translation: Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero
Prologue
In the language of India: Bodhisattvacharyavatara.
In the language of Tibet: Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero.
I bow down to all the Buddhas and awakening heroes.
Chapter One: Explaining the Benefits of the Awakening Mind

I bow down with respect to the Well-Gone Ones who have the truth body, and to their children. I also bow to everyone who deserves respect. I will briefly explain how to keep the promises of the children of the Well-Gone One. I will explain this by following the sacred texts.
I am not saying anything new here. I am also not very good at writing. Because of this, I did not write this to help others. I wrote this just to train my own mind.
To practice good deeds, the power of my faith will grow for a while through these words. If other people who are as lucky as me see them, these words will become meaningful.

This free and fortunate life is very hard to find. We have gained what we need to reach the purpose of a human life. If we do not use this life to do what is helpful, how will we ever find it perfectly again?

On a dark night covered in thick clouds, a flash of lightning makes everything bright for a second. In the same way, by the power of the Buddha, the mind to build a store of goodness rarely appears in the world. It only happens once in a hundred times.
Because of this, a good deed is always weak. But harmful deeds are very strong and hard to bear. Besides the awakening mind for full awakening, what other good deed could ever defeat them?
Even if you have done a terrible harmful deed, this mind will free you in an instant. It is like relying on a brave hero to escape great fear. Why wouldn't careful people rely on it?
It is like the fire at the end of time. It completely burns up great mistakes in a single instant. The wise Protector Maitreya explained its endless benefits to Sudhana.
In short, you should know that the awakening mind has two types. They are the mind that wishes to awaken and the mind that sets out to awaken.
Think about the difference between wanting to go somewhere and actually going. A wise person should understand the difference between these two minds in the exact same way.
The mind that wishes to awaken brings a great result in the cycle of rebirth. But a store of goodness does not grow from it continuously. That only happens with the mind that sets out to awaken.
You might truly take up this mind to completely free the endless realm of living beings. You make this choice with a mind of never turning back. From that very moment...
Most people do not have this wish even for themselves. But this wish to help every living being is born as a brand new wonder. It is an amazing jewel of a mind.
This mind brings joy to all beings. It is the medicine for the suffering of living beings. How could anyone ever measure the store of goodness of such a precious mind?
Just wishing to help is better than making offerings to the Buddhas. So, what need is there to mention working hard for the happiness of every single living being?
People want to throw away their suffering, but they run right into it. They want happiness. But because of ignorance, they destroy their own happiness as if it were an enemy.
Some people have no happiness and face so much suffering. This mind fills them with happiness and cuts through all their suffering.
It even clears away their ignorance. Where is there a good deed equal to that? Where is there a friend like that? Where is there a store of goodness like that?
From this moment on, a huge store of goodness keeps growing. It happens even if I am asleep or acting with carelessness. It never stops, and it is as big as space.
The Thus-Gone One himself explained this. He gave the reasons for it in the teaching called the Question of Subahu. He said this to help living beings who are just starting out.
If someone just thinks, 'I will cure the headaches of every living being,' they have a kind wish. They gain an immeasurable store of goodness.
What if someone wants to take away the immeasurable pain of every living being? What if they want to build up immeasurable good qualities for each one? We do not even need to ask how great that is!
Who else has such a kind wish? Does a father or even a mother have it? Do the gods or a wise seer? Does even Brahma have this wish?
Before now, those living beings never dreamed of this kind of wish for themselves. So how could they ever have it for anyone else?
The Lords of Sages thought deeply for many great ages. They saw that only this is helpful. With it, countless beings will easily find the greatest happiness.

Some people want to end the hundreds of sufferings of life. Some want to take away the sadness of living beings. Others want to enjoy hundreds of joys. All of them should never give up the awakening mind.

As soon as the awakening mind is born, everything changes in a flash. Poor beings trapped in the prison of the cycle of rebirth will be called children of the Well-Gone Ones. The whole world, including gods and humans, will bow down to them.
It is like the very best gold-making potion. It takes this impure body and turns it into the priceless jewel of a Victorious One's body. Therefore, hold tightly to the awakening mind.

The one leader of travelers for all beings has a limitless mind. He looked at it closely and saw how precious it is. Anyone who wants to leave the homes of beings should hold tightly to the precious awakening mind.
All other good deeds are like a banana tree. After giving a result, they are used up. But the tree of the awakening mind always gives a result. It never runs out, and it keeps growing.
People praise someone who pays back a favor. So we should definitely praise the awakening hero who does good things without even being asked.
Think about someone who feeds a few beings. They might just give one quick meal. They might even be mean while feeding them. Still, people honor them for doing a good deed.

Now think of someone who gives the greatest happiness of the Well-Gone Ones to countless living beings for a long time. They give constantly to make every wish come true. Imagine how wonderful that person is!
What if someone thinks bad thoughts about such a kind child of the Victorious Ones? The Sage taught that for every bad thought, they will stay in hell for a great age.
But if someone feels deep respect for them, the result is even greater. Even in hard times, a child of the Victorious Ones does no harmful deeds. Their good deeds just naturally grow.
I bow down to anyone who has grown this perfect, precious mind. Even if someone hurts them, they still connect that person to happiness. I go for shelter to these sources of happiness.
I imagine lakes and ponds filled with lotuses. Beautiful swans sing sweetly there. I picture everything out to the edge of endless space that belongs to no one.
In my mind, I gather all these things. I offer them to the Sages and their children. They are the ones worthy of gifts. May those of great compassion think of me with love and accept my offerings.
I have no store of goodness, and I am very poor. I have no other wealth to offer. Therefore, may the Protectors who care about the good of others accept this for my sake.
I offer my whole body forever to the Victorious Ones and their children. O greatest heroes, please accept me completely. With deep respect, I will serve you.
Because you have accepted me, I will be brave in this life. I will help all living beings. I will leave behind my past harmful deeds. From now on, I will not do any more harmful deeds.
I picture wonderful, sweet-smelling bathhouses. They have clear and shining crystal floors. Beautiful pillars made of bright jewels hold them up. Sparkling covers made of pearls are spread above.
I offer a bath to the Thus-Gone Ones and their children. I use many beautiful vases full of sweet, scented water. I give this bath with lots of songs and music.
I dry their bodies with clean, beautiful cloths that smell like perfume. Then I offer them the very best robes. These robes are perfectly colored and smell wonderful.
I will also decorate the noble Samantabhadra, Manjushri, Avalokiteshvara, and others. I will use many fine clothes that are thin and soft. I will give them hundreds of the very best ornaments.
I will rub the best perfumes on the bodies of all the Lords of Sages. The sweet smell spreads through the whole world of three thousand worlds. Their bodies shine and glow like polished gold.

I make offerings to the Lords of Sages, the best ones worthy of offerings. I offer beautiful heavenly flowers, lotuses, blue lotuses, and all other sweet-smelling flowers. I also offer them beautiful flower garlands that are strung together perfectly.
I offer them thick clouds of smoke from the very best incense. The wonderful smell fills the air. I will also give them a feast of the gods, made of many different foods and drinks.
This is the first chapter from Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero. It is called Explaining the Benefits of the Awakening Mind.
Chapter Two: Confessing Harmful Deeds

I want to take hold of that precious mind. So I make wonderful offerings to the Thus-Gone Ones and the holy teachings. I make offerings to the spotless Jewel and to the children of the Buddhas. They are oceans of good qualities.
I offer all the flowers and fruits there are. I offer every kind of medicine. I offer all the jewels in the world and all the pure, pleasing water.
I offer mountains made of jewels. I offer quiet and delightful forests. I offer trees decorated with beautiful flowers. I offer trees with branches bending down from excellent fruit.

I offer sweet smells and incense from the worlds of gods and others. I offer wish-granting trees and jewel trees. I offer crops that grow without being planted. I offer every other beautiful thing that is worthy of being offered.
I will offer precious lamps inside rows of golden lotuses. I will scatter lovely flowers on the smooth, sweet-smelling ground.

I also offer palaces beyond measure that echo with beautiful songs of praise. They shine brightly with hanging pearls and jewels, decorating the endless sky. I offer these to those whose nature is compassion.

I offer beautiful jeweled umbrellas with golden handles. They have lovely decorations all around. They are perfectly shaped, wonderful to look at, and held high. I will always offer these to the Lords of Sages.
I also give many other offerings along with beautiful, sweet music. May clouds that soothe the suffering of living beings stay in all these places.
May a rain of jewels, flowers, and other gifts fall without stopping upon all the jewels of the holy teachings. May it also fall upon the shrines and statues.
Just as Manjushri and others make offerings to the Victorious Ones, I do the same. I make offerings to the Thus-Gone Ones, the Protectors, and their children.
I praise those who are an ocean of good qualities. I praise them with oceans of beautiful songs. May clouds of this sweet music rise up everywhere for them.

I bow down to every Buddha of the past, present and future. I bow down to the teachings and the Supreme Assembly. I imagine having as many bodies as all the atoms in the land. All of my bodies bow down.
I bow down to every basis of the awakening mind and to the shrines. I bow down to the teacher who ordained me and to my other teachers. I also bow down to every person of strict practice.
Until I reach the heart of awakening, the Buddhas are who I go to for shelter. I also look to the teachings and the assembly of awakening heroes for shelter.
I put my hands together and pray. I pray to the fully awakened Buddhas who live in all directions. I pray to those with the awakening mind. They all have great compassion.
I have lived in this cycle of rebirth with no beginning. In this life and in past lives, I have done harmful deeds without knowing it. I have also made others do harmful deeds.
Sometimes ignorance confused me. I used to feel joy in my mistakes. Now I see how wrong they were. I own up to them to the Protectors from the bottom of my heart.
I have done harm to the Three Jewels, my parents, and my teachers. Driven by a troubling emotion, I harmed them with my body, my speech, and my mind.
I am stained by many faults. As one who has done harmful deeds, I have done terrible things. I own up to every harmful deed to the Guides.
I might die before the cleansing of my harmful deeds. Please protect me quickly so I can have sure freedom from them.
The Lord of Death cannot be trusted. He does not wait to see if our work is done or not. Whether we are sick or healthy, no one can trust this life. It can end suddenly.
I did not understand that I must go and leave everything behind. For the sake of friends and enemies, I have done many kinds of harmful deeds.
Enemies will disappear. Friends will disappear. I will disappear too. Everything will fade away.
Just like a dream, everything I have enjoyed will become only a memory. Nothing from the past will be seen again.
Even in this life, many friends and enemies have passed away. The terrible harmful deeds I did for them are what stay with me.
I did not understand that I will not last forever. Because of ignorance, clinging, and hatred, I have done many kinds of harmful deeds.
Day and night, my time alive is always running out. Since no more time is ever added, why would someone like me not die?
When I lie on my bed, my family and friends might surround me. But I alone will feel my life ending.
When the messengers of Yama grab me, how can my family and friends help? If only a store of goodness can keep me safe at that time, I have not relied on even that.
O Protectors, I did not know about these terrors because of my carelessness. For the sake of this not lasting life, I have done many harmful deeds.
Even a person being led away today to have their limbs cut off is terrified. Their mouth is dry and their eyes are upset. They look completely changed from how they were before.
So what about someone grabbed by the messengers of Yama with their terrifying bodies? They are struck by the sickness of great fear. There is no need to even mention their complete misery.
I will ask, "Who will really protect me from this great terror?" My eyes will be wide open in panic. I will search the four directions for a shelter.
I will see no shelter in the four directions. Then I will fall into deep despair. If there is no shelter in that place, what will I do at that time?
From this very day, the Victorious Ones are the ones I go to for shelter. They are the Protectors of beings. They work hard to keep beings safe. These strong ones chase away all fears.
In the same way, their teachings are what I go to for shelter. These teachings chase away the fears of the cycle of rebirth. The group of awakening heroes is also who I go to for shelter.
I am terrified by fear. So, I offer myself to Samantabhadra. I also give my body to Manjushri.
His actions are always perfect because of his compassion. I cry out in a sad voice to the protector Avalokiteshvara. I say, 'Please protect me, one who has done harmful deeds!'
Looking for shelter, I cry out from my heart to noble Akashagarbha. I also call to Kshitigarbha. I cry out to every Protector who has great compassion.
The Thunderbolt-holder is the one I go to for shelter. When the messengers of Yama and other harmful beings see him, they are terrified. They run away in all four directions.
Who has made me safe from fear? How will I make sure I escape from this? If I will definitely stop existing one day, how can my mind be at peace?
Everything I felt in the past is gone. What is left of it for me? Because I held on to those things so tightly, I broke the teacher's commands.
I will have to leave this life behind. I will also leave my family and friends. If I must go somewhere completely alone, what is the use of having friends or enemies?
Suffering comes from a bad deed. I must ask myself how I will ever escape from that. It is right for me to think only about this question all day and all night.
I lacked understanding and was full of ignorance. Because of this, I have done deeds wrong in themselves. I have also done forbidden harmful deeds. I have committed all of these.
Right in front of the Protectors, I stand with my hands pressed together. My mind is terrified of suffering. I bow down again and again, and I own up to all of those.
I pray that the Guides see my harmful deeds as faults. Because this is not good, I will never do it again.
From Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero, the second chapter: Confessing Harmful Deeds.
Chapter Three: Completely Adopting the Awakening Mind
I joyfully rejoice in the good deeds of all living beings that bring rest from the suffering of the unhappy realms. I also rejoice when suffering beings find happiness.

I rejoice in the gathered good deeds that lead to awakening. I rejoice in the complete freedom of beings with a body from the suffering of the cycle of rebirth. I rejoice in the awakening of the Protectors. I also rejoice in the levels of the children of the Victorious Ones.
I joyfully rejoice in the ocean of good deeds from the birth of the awakening mind, which brings happiness to all living beings. I also rejoice in the actions that help living beings.
In the past, I broke your rules. Now I have seen great danger. You are who I go to for shelter. Please take away my fears quickly!
If we are scared of a normal illness, we must follow the doctor's orders. So of course we must when we are always sick! We have a disease made of a hundred faults like longing.
Just one of these faults can destroy all the people living in Jambudvipa. No other medicine can cure them. We cannot find a cure anywhere at all.
The All-Knowing Doctor takes away all pain. Not wanting to follow his orders is extreme ignorance. Anyone who ignores him should be scolded.
We must be careful even near a small, normal cliff. So of course we must be careful near a huge drop! We could fall a thousand leagues and be trapped for a long time.
It is wrong for me to relax and think, 'I will not die today.' The time when I will be gone will definitely come.
Because of my unknowing and ignorance, I have done bad things. I have committed deeds wrong in themselves. I have also done all kinds of forbidden harmful deeds.
I put my hands together and pray to the Buddhas everywhere. Living beings are lost in the dark with their suffering. Please light the lamp of the teachings for them.
I put my hands together and pray to the Victorious Ones who wish to pass into freedom from sorrow. Do not leave these blind wandering beings behind. Please stay with us for countless great ages.
By all the good deeds I have gathered in this way, may the suffering of every living being be taken away completely.
As long as any beings are sick, may I help them until they are cured. May I be their medicine, their doctor, and their nurse.
May I rain down food and drink to take away the suffering of hunger and thirst. During the middle great age of famine, may I become food and drink myself.
For every living being who is poor and has nothing, may I become a treasure that never runs out. May I stay right in front of them as everything they need.
I will freely give away my body and my belongings. I will give away my good deeds from the past, present and future. I will do this without feeling a loss to help all living beings.
Giving up everything brings freedom from sorrow. My mind wants to reach this freedom from sorrow. Since I must give up everything anyway, it is best to give it to living beings.
I have already given this body to all beings with a body for their happiness. Let them do whatever they please with it. They can hit it, insult it, or even kill it.
They can play with my body. They can laugh at it and make fun of it. Since I have already given this body away, why should I take care of it?
Let them do any action to me, as long as it does not hurt them. Whenever anyone focuses on me, may it always be helpful to them. May it never be useless.
When people focus on me, they might feel anger or faith. May those very feelings always help them. May that anger or faith be the reason they reach all their goals.
If people say bad things about me, hurt me, or make fun of me, may they all have the good fortune of awakening.
May I become a Protector for anyone who has no Protector. May I be a guide for travelers on the path. For those who want to cross over, may I become a boat, a ship, and a bridge.
May I be an island for those who seek an island. May I be a resting place for those who want to rest. For any being with a body who wants a servant, may I become a servant to them all.
May I become a wish-fulfilling jewel and a wonderful vase. May I become powerful sacred words and a great medicine. May I be wish-granting trees and a wish-granting cow for every being with a body.
Just like the earth and the other basic elements, and just like space, may I always be a ground that supports countless living beings in many different ways.
In the same way, reaching to the very edges of space, may I support the whole realm of living beings in every way. May I sustain them until they all reach freedom from sorrow.
In the past, the Well-Gone Ones created the awakening mind. Step by step, they followed the trainings of the awakening heroes.
In the same way, I will create the awakening mind to help wandering beings. Step by step, I will also practice the trainings.
A wise person takes hold of the awakening mind with clear faith. To make it grow even more, they should encourage their mind like this:
Today my life has great meaning. I have gained a good human life. Today I am born into the family of the Buddhas. Today I have become a child of the Buddhas.
Now I must do everything I can to act like my new family. I will act well so that I never bring shame to this pure and noble family.
Imagine a blind person finding a precious jewel in a pile of trash. By that same amazing luck, this awakening mind has been born in me.
From Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero, the third chapter, called "Fully Taking Hold of the Awakening Mind."
Chapter Four: Teaching Carefulness
A child of the Victorious Ones has firmly taken hold of the awakening mind in this way. They should always try hard not to break the trainings.
If something is started without thinking, or not checked carefully, you should think about whether to do it or drop it. This is true even if a promise was made.
The Buddhas and their children have checked this with great wisdom. I have also checked it again and again. So what reason do I have to delay it?
If I make a promise like that but do not act on it, I am tricking all those living beings. What sort of wandering being will I become?
It is the best nectar that defeats the Lord of Death for beings. It is the treasure that never runs out, taking away the poverty of beings.
It is the best medicine that cures the illnesses of beings. It is a tree of rest for beings who are tired from wandering the path of life.
It is a bridge for everyone that frees all beings from the unhappy realms. It is the rising moon of the mind that clears away the pain of beings' troubling emotions.
It is the great sun that clears the dimness of beings' not knowing. It is the rich butter made by churning the milk of the holy teachings.
Beings are guests traveling the path of life who wish to enjoy happiness. This is the greatest happiness waiting nearby. It satisfies the great guests, the living beings.
Today, in front of all the Protectors, I have invited beings as guests to the state of a Well-Gone One, and to happiness in the meantime. Let gods, demigods, and others rejoice!
Suppose powerful falls and the powerful awakening mind take turns in the cycle of rebirth. Then it will take a long time to reach the stages.
Because of this, I must carefully do what I promised. If I do not make an effort starting today, I will go lower and lower.
Countless Buddhas have passed away while helping all living beings. But because of my own faults, I have not been healed by them.
If I keep acting this way, the same things will happen again and again. I will be sick, tied up, and cut in the unhappy realms.
A Thus-Gone One appearing is very rare. Getting a human body, having trust, and being ready to do good deeds are also rare. When will I ever get these things again?
Today I am not sick. I have food and I am safe from harm. Even so, life can trick me in an instant. My body is just like a short loan.
Suppose you promise in your mind to give away a small, ordinary thing. If you do not give it, teachings say you will become a hungry ghost.
I have sincerely invited every being to the greatest happiness. If I trick them now, how can I ever go to a happy realm?
Even if someone gives up the awakening mind, they might still find freedom. This is a mysterious result of action. Only the All-Knowing One understands it.
For an awakening hero, giving this up is the heaviest fall of all. If this happens, you fail to help all living beings.
Someone might block this hero's store of goodness for even a single moment. This stops the hero from helping living beings. Because of this, their time in an unhappy realm will be endless.

Destroying the happiness of a single living being will bring my own ruin. What if I destroy the happiness of every being with a body? They fill all of space to its very edge. We do not even need to ask!
If I act like this, I will not even get a human body. If I do not get a human body, I will only do harmful deeds and no good deeds.
Right now I have the chance to do good deeds. If I do not do them, what will I be able to do later? I will be completely confused by the suffering of the unhappy realms.
If I do not do good deeds and only gather harmful deeds, things will be bad. I will not even hear about the happy realms for a billion great ages.
For this reason, the Blessed One said that being human is extremely hard to achieve. He said it is like a turtle poking its neck through the hole of a wooden yoke drifting on a great ocean.
Just one instant of a harmful deed can trap me in Avichi for a great age. I have gathered harmful deeds in the cycle of rebirth, which has no beginning. So of course I will not go to a happy realm!
I will not win freedom just by living through that. While I am experiencing it, I will just create other harmful deeds.
I have found this freedom to practice. If I do not build a habit of doing good deeds, there is no worse trick than this. There is no worse confusion than this.
If I understand this but stay lazy because I am confused, great sorrow will come to me when it is time to die.
If the unbearable fire of hell burns my body for a long time, my mind will surely be tormented by the blazing fire of unbearable regret.
This helpful state is very hard to find. Somehow, I have found it by chance. But what if, even while I understand this, I am led back again to that hell?
It is as if I have been confused by sacred words. I am left with no mind here. I do not even know what is confusing me. What is inside me?
My enemies, like hatred and wanting, do not have hands or feet. They are not brave or wise. So how have they made me like a slave?
These enemies live right inside my mind. They hurt me whenever they want. If I do not get angry at them and just practice patience, that is the wrong kind of patience. I should be scolded for it.
Even if all the gods and demigods rose up against me as enemies, they could not drag me away. They could not throw me into the fire of the Avichi hell.
But my powerful enemy, these troubling emotions, can throw me there in a single instant. If Mount Meru touched that fire, it would burn away without leaving even ashes.
My troubling emotions are enemies that last a very long time. They seem to have no beginning and no end. All my other enemies could never last that long.
If I serve and honor my other enemies, they might bring me help and happiness. But if I serve my troubling emotions, they only bring me more suffering and harm.

These enemies have stayed with me for a long time without stopping. They are the only reason I suffer so many harms. If they truly live inside my heart, how could I be fearless and happy in the cycle of rebirth?
These inner enemies guard the prison of the cycle of rebirth. They become executioners in hell. If they stay inside my mind in a net of clinging, how could I ever be happy?

So, until I completely destroy this enemy, I will not give up my effort. Think of people who are filled with pride. If someone wrongs them just a little, they get angry. They do not sleep until they have destroyed that enemy.

In battle, soldiers fight enemies who will die a natural death anyway. These soldiers ignore the suffering of being struck by arrows, spears, and weapons. They do not turn back and run away without reaching their goal.

My true natural enemies are the constant cause of all suffering. Today, I am trying hard to destroy them. Even if this fight causes me hundreds of sufferings, it will certainly not make me despair and lose heart.
People sometimes wear scars from meaningless fights with enemies like decorations on their bodies. I am working hard to achieve a truly great goal. Why should suffering be a harm to me?

Fishermen, outcasts, farmers, and others only think about making a living. Yet they put up with the pain of cold and heat. I am working for the happiness of all wandering beings. Why should someone like me not endure these things too?

I promised to free the wandering beings who fill space in the ten directions. I promised to free them from their troubling emotions. But when I made this promise, I was not even free from my own troubling emotions!
Since I do not even know what I can really do, am I not crazy to talk like this? Still, I will never turn back from destroying my troubling emotions.
I will hold tightly to this goal. I will hold a grudge and fight this battle! This is the only kind of troubling emotion I should not let go of, because it destroys all other troubling emotions.
Even if I am burned and killed, so be it. Even if my head is cut off, that is fine. But I will never bow down to my enemies, the troubling emotions.
When normal enemies are chased out of a country, they go live in other lands. They build up their strength and come back. But my enemies, the troubling emotions, are not like that.

These awful troubling emotions can be cleared away by the eye of wisdom. Once they are chased out of my mind, where will they go? Where could they hide to come back and hurt me? The truth is just that my mind is weak and I am not trying hard enough.

Troubling emotions do not live in the things we sense. They do not live in the group of senses, or in between. If they are nowhere else, where do they stay to harm all beings? They are like an illusion. So, let go of fear in your heart and work hard to know them. Why do I hurt myself for no reason in the hells and other places?
Thinking like this, I will work hard. I will do the training just as it was taught. If a sick person does not listen to the doctor, how can medicine cure them?
The fourth chapter from Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero, called Carefulness.
Chapter Five: Guarding Watchfulness
If you want to guard the training, you must guard your mind well. If this mind is not guarded, you cannot guard the training at all.
Letting the elephant of the mind run wild causes harm in the Avichi hell. A wild, crazy elephant here does not cause that much harm.
Having just one clear mind brings a great result. It can make you like Brahma. But if your actions are weak, just using your body and words will not bring a result like that.
You might do recitation and hard practice for a long time. But if you do them with a wandering mind, they are meaningless. The Knower of the way things really are said this.

Some people do not know the most important part of the teachings. They do not know this secret of the mind. They want to find happiness and end suffering. But they will just wander around for no reason.
Because of this, I will carefully hold and protect this mind of mine. What is the point of doing many kinds of strict practice? The only one I need is the strict practice of guarding the mind.
If you are in a wild crowd, you carefully protect a bodily wound. In the same way, when you are around bad people, you must always protect this wound of the mind.
A person carefully protects a scratch because they fear the small suffering of a wound. So why do people who fear the Crushing Hell and Destroying hell not guard the wound of the mind?
If I tightly tie up the elephant of the mind with the rope of keeping in mind, all fears will disappear. Every good deed will come right into my hands.
There are tigers, lions, elephants, bears, snakes, and all enemies. There are hell guardians, witches, and also demons.
If I tie up this mind alone, all of those things are tied up. If I tame this mind alone, all of them are tamed.
All fears and endless suffering come from the mind. This is what the Speaker of Truth himself has taught.
Who purposely made the weapons in the hell of living beings? Who created the burning iron ground? Where did those groups of women come from?
The Sage taught that all these things come from a harmful mind. So, in the three worlds, there is no other fear besides the mind.
If the perfection of giving means taking away the poverty of all beings, how did the past Protectors reach perfection? There are still poor beings today.
The perfection of giving is taught as having the mind of giving everything away. It means wanting to give all your things and their good results to everyone. Therefore, it is just the mind itself.
Where could fish and other animals be put so they are never killed? The perfection of good conduct comes from getting the mind of giving up harmful actions.
Wild living beings are as endless as space. They can never be fully defeated. But if this single mind of anger is defeated, it is like defeating all those enemies at once.
How could there ever be enough leather to cover the whole earth? But with just enough leather for the soles of your shoes, it is as if the whole earth is covered.
In the same way, I cannot stop every outside thing. I will just stop this mind of mine. What need is there to stop anything else?
If a person acts like this, they will stay strong. Whether living among bad people or among women, a steady person of self-restraint will not fail.
It is better to lose my gain and honor. It is better to lose my body and my life. It is even better to lose other good deeds. But I must never let my mind fail.
To those who want to guard the mind, I put my hands together and ask this. Guard both keeping in mind and watchfulness with all your effort!
People who are troubled by illness have no power to do anything. In the same way, a mind troubled by confusion has no power to do anything.
If someone has a mind without watchfulness, what they hear, think about, and practice will leak out. Like water in a cracked pot, it does not stay in keeping in mind.
Many people have learning and faith. Many people work hard with great effort. But if they make the mistake of lacking watchfulness, they will be stained by a fall.
When keeping in mind stays at the door of the mind to guard it, watchfulness will come. Even what was lost will come back.
First, when I see that a mind like this has faults, I should stay firm like a log of wood.
I should never look around for no reason. With a firm mind, I should always look down.
To rest my eyes, I should sometimes look around. If I see someone, I should look at them and say, "Welcome."
To check for danger on the path, I should keep looking in all four directions. After resting, I should turn and look behind me.
After checking in front and behind me, I should go forward or go back. In the same way, I should always understand what is needed before I act.
When keeping in mind fades away, the thieves of lost watchfulness sneak in. Even if I have gathered a store of goodness, they rob me. Then I go down to an unhappy realm.
This gang of thieves, made of troubling emotions, looks for a chance to strike. When they find it, they steal every good deed. They even destroy life in a happy realm.
So, I must never let keeping in mind wander away from the door of the mind. If it does leave, I should remember the pain of the unhappy realms and bring it right back.
For lucky people who act with careful respect, keeping in mind grows easily. This happens by spending time with a teacher and listening to the teacher who ordained me.
The Buddhas and awakening heroes can see everywhere without anything blocking their view. I should think, "I am always standing right in front of them all."
Thinking this way, I should act with shame, respect, and fear. By doing this, keeping the Buddha in mind will happen to me again and again.
When I start an action, I should think, 'My body will stay like this.' Then I should check it sometimes. I should ask, 'How is my body staying?'
I must try with all my effort to watch the mad elephant of the mind. I must tie it to the great pillar of thinking about the teachings so it does not escape.
I must try hard not to lose my deep focus for even a single moment. To do this, I must carefully check my mind. I should ask, 'What is my mind doing?'

When I face danger or go to a festival, I might not be able to do everything perfectly. If so, I should just relax. It is taught that at times of giving, good conduct should be treated with even-mindedness.
When I plan to do something and start it, I should not think of anything else. I should keep my thoughts on it. I must finish that very thing first.
If I act this way, everything is done well. Otherwise, neither task will be finished. In this way, the secondary troubling emotion of lacking watchfulness will not grow.
If I want gain, honor, or fame, or if I want to seek helpers and followers. If my mind wants to be served, at that time I should stay like a log.
If my mind wants to drop the good of others to seek my own good, or if it just wants to speak, then I should stay like a log.
When impatience, laziness, and fear appear, along with rudeness and idle talk. Or if a mind attached to my own side comes up, at that time I should stay like a log.
I must check my mind for any troubling emotion and for chasing meaningless things. At that time, a hero should use a remedy to hold the mind firmly.
With strong certainty and deep trust, I should be steady, respectful, and polite. With a sense of shame and a fear of doing wrong, I should be peaceful and try hard to make others happy.

I should not be upset by the clashing desires of any childish person. Instead, I should think, "This mind of theirs has appeared because a troubling emotion grew in them." I will be a compassionate one.
There are many kinds of silly talk and amazing shows. When I join in these things, I must stop clinging to them.
If I dig the earth, cut grass, or draw lines on the ground for no reason, I should remember the training of the Well-Gone One. Out of fear, I should stop right away.
Whenever I want to move or even speak, I should check my own mind first. Then I should act firmly and do the right thing.
Whenever my mind has clinging or wants to feel anger, I should not act or speak. I should stay perfectly still, like a log.
I might feel restlessness or mockery. I might have pride and arrogance. I might think about exposing others' faults. I might have sneakiness or a deceiving mind.
Whenever I am focused on praising myself or putting others down, or if I say mean things and feel regret, at that time I should stay just like a log.
Take apart even the bones. Look right down to the marrow. Check for yourself. What essence is really in there?
You look so hard, but you find no essence. Why do you still protect this body with clinging?
Filth is not fit for you to eat. Blood is not fit to drink. Guts are not fit to suck. So what will this body do for you?
At best, it is only guarded as food for foxes and vultures. Every human body is just something to be put to use.
You might guard it carefully. But the cruel Lord of Death will snatch it away. He will give it to birds and dogs. What can you do then?
You would not give clothes to a servant who cannot work. This body will leave you even if you feed it well. Why wear yourself out taking care of it?
When I do things that are free of blame with myself and any living being, I must always hold my mind like a magical creation. It must not have any 'I' in it.
It took a long time to get this best chance to practise. I should think about this again and again. I must keep my mind as steady and unshakable as Mount Meru.
When hungry vultures drag this dead body all around, you are not upset, my mind. So why do you care so much for it right now?
My mind, you hold onto this body and call it 'mine'. But why do you guard it so closely? You and the body are completely separate. What can it really do for you?
My mind of confusion, why do you not hold onto a clean wooden shape instead? This body is just a machine made of filth. What is the use of guarding this rotten thing?
First, use your own thinking mind to separate this layer of skin. Then, use the blade of wisdom to separate the flesh from the web of bones.
I pay my body what it needs, like a worker. Then I make it work for my goals. I should not give it everything if it brings no benefit.
I think of my body as just a boat for moving around. To help living beings, I will turn it into a wish-granting body.
By being in control of myself, I will always keep a smiling face. I will completely stop frowning and scowling. I will be a friend to beings and speak honestly.
I will not recklessly throw down chairs and other things with noise. I will not open doors with force. I will always enjoy acting quietly.
Herons, cats, and thieves get what they want by moving silently and secretly. The Sage should always act in that same way.
Some people give good advice, and others say helpful things without being asked. I will accept their words with respect, placing them on my head like a crown. I will always be a student to everyone.
Sometimes I feel like praising myself or putting others down. I might say mean things and feel full of regret. At those times, I should stay still like a log.
When someone says something good, I should tell them they spoke well! If I see someone building a store of goodness, I should happily praise them.

I should talk about people's good qualities when they are not around. If others talk about a good quality, I should join in. If they talk about my own good qualities, I should just know they recognize a good quality.
Everything we do is to find joy. True joy is rare even if you try to buy it. So, I should enjoy the happiness of joy by looking at the good qualities others have gained.
I lose nothing in this life, and I will have great happiness in the next. Through faults, there is sadness and suffering now. In the next life, there is great suffering.
When I speak, my words should make sense and bring comfort. My meaning should be clear and pleasing. I must let go of clinging and hatred. I should speak gently and not say too much.
When I look at living beings, I should think, "By relying on these very beings, I will become a Buddha." I should always look at them in a direct and loving way.
A good deed becomes very great when you do it with a strong, lasting wish, or as a remedy. This is true when you act toward people with good qualities, people who help you, and those in suffering.
I will become skilled and full of faith. I will always do my work myself. I should not rely on anyone else for any action at all.

I should practice the perfection of giving and the other practices better and better over time. I should not give up something big for something small. Above all, I must think about the good of others.
Knowing this, I must always work hard for the good of others. The Compassionate One sees far ahead. Because of this, he allows a person working for others to do even forbidden things.

I should share with people in miserable states, people with no protection, and those doing strict practice. I should eat only the right amount. I must give away everything except my three monk's robes.
My body practices the holy teachings. I should not harm it for something small. If I act like this, I will quickly fulfill the wishes of every living being.
So, work on being in control of oneself. Always keep a smiling face. Stop frowning and scowling completely. Be a friend to wandering beings and speak honestly.
If my compassion is not pure, I should not give away my body. I should only give it away if it will help achieve a great purpose in this life and future lives.

I should not share the teachings with disrespectful people. I should not teach people who wrap their heads unless they are sick. I must not teach anyone holding an umbrella, a stick, or a weapon, or those with covered heads.
I should not share deep and vast teachings with people who are not ready. I should not teach a woman when no man is present. I must always show equal respect to both simple and highest teachings.

People who are ready for the vast teachings should not practice the lesser teachings instead. Good behavior should not be given up completely. I should not trick people with teaching texts and sacred words.
When I spit or throw away sticks used to clean teeth, I should cover them up. It is wrong to pee or leave waste in water or on land that people use.
I should not eat with my mouth full, make noises, or chew with my mouth wide open. I should not sit with my legs stretched out, and I should not rub my hands together.

I should not be alone with another woman in a vehicle, on a bed, on a seat, or in a room. By watching and asking questions, I should find out what upsets people. Then I must avoid doing anything that causes the world to lose faith.
I should never point with just one finger. Instead, I should respectfully use my whole right hand. Even when I am just showing someone the way to go, I should point like this.
I should not wave my hands around too much. I should move them just a little and make a sound, like snapping my fingers, to signal someone. Otherwise, I will lose my self-control.

I should lie down facing the direction I want, just like the Protector lay when passing into freedom from sorrow. Right from the very start, I should use watchfulness. I must firmly set my mind on waking up quickly.
The teachings say that the way of acting of the awakening hero is endless. Until I am able to do all of it, I must certainly practice actions that make my mind pure.
Three times during the day and three times at night, I should recite the Three Heaps text. By relying on the Victorious Ones and the awakening mind, I will clear away my remaining falls.
Whether I am acting on my own or following someone else, I should always try hard. No matter what I am doing, I must follow whatever I was taught as a training.
There is no action that is not a training for a child of the Victorious Ones. For a wise person who lives like this, everything becomes a store of goodness.
Whether directly or indirectly, I should only do things that help living beings. For the sake of living beings alone, I give everything to awakening by sharing the goodness.
I must never give up a friend who guides me, even to save my own life. This friend knows the meaning of the Great Vehicle and keeps the highest strict practice of the awakening heroes.
I should learn how to rely on a teacher from the life story of Shrisambhava. I will know this and other things spoken by the Buddha by reading the scriptures.
The trainings are found in the scriptures, so I must read the scriptures. I should look at the Teaching of Akashagarbha first of all.
I must also read the Compendium of Trainings again and again. It shows in great detail what I need to practice all the time.
Or, for now, I should read the short Collection of the Buddha's Talks. I must also try hard to read both teaching texts written by the noble Nagarjuna.
I should practice whatever is not forbidden in them. To protect the minds of the world, I must see the training and practice perfectly.
I must check the states of my body and mind again and again. In short, this alone is the meaning of guarding watchfulness.
I must actually do these things with my body. What good is just saying the words? Will a sick person get well just by reading a medical book?
From Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero, the fifth chapter: Guarding Watchfulness.
Chapter Six: Teaching Patience
A single moment of anger destroys all your good actions. It wipes out what you gathered over a thousand great ages, like giving and making offerings to the Well-Gone Ones.
There is no harmful deed quite like hatred. There is no hard practice quite like patience. Because of this, you should try your best to practice meditation on patience in many different ways.
If you hold hatred like a sharp dart in your mind, your mind will not feel peace. You will not find joy or happiness. You will not sleep, and you will feel unsteady.
Think of the people who depend on a master for wealth and honor. If that master is full of hatred, even those people will attack and try to kill him.
Because of it, friends feel sad. Even if he tries to gather them by giving, they will not stay. In short, there is no such thing as a happy person who holds onto anger.
The enemy of anger produces these and other kinds of suffering. Whoever tries hard to destroy anger will be happy in this life and the next.
Hatred grows when things happen that I do not want, or when I am stopped from getting what I want. This gives hatred the food of unhappiness. Then it grows strong and destroys me.
Therefore, I must completely destroy the food of that enemy. This enemy has no other job except to hurt me.
Whatever happens, I will not upset my joyful mind. Even if I am unhappy, it does not get me what I want. It only makes my good deeds fade away.
If a problem can be fixed, why be unhappy about it? If it cannot be fixed, what is the use of being unhappy?
I do not want suffering, disrespect, harsh words, or a bad name for myself or for my friends. But for an enemy, it is the exact opposite.
The causes of happiness only happen sometimes. The causes of suffering are very common. Without suffering, there is no wish to be free. So, my mind, you must be strong.
Followers of Durga and the Karnapas put up with the feeling of being burned and cut. They do this for no real reason. So why should I not endure pain for the sake of freedom?
Everything becomes easier when you get used to it. There is nothing in the world that does not. So, by getting used to small harms, you can learn to endure great harms.
Think of snakes and biting flies. Think of the feeling of hunger and thirst. Think of itchy rashes. Why do you not see that all this suffering is pointless?
I will not be too sensitive to heat, cold, rain, or wind. I will not complain about sickness, being tied up, or being hit. If I am too sensitive, the harm only gets worse.
When some people see their own blood, they become extra brave and strong. But when other people see someone else's blood, they get dizzy and faint.
This comes from a steady mind or from being a coward. So, ignore harm. Do not let suffering upset you.
Even when suffering happens, wise people keep a clear mind. They are fighting a war against troubling emotions. Many harms happen during a battle.
Real heroes ignore all suffering. They defeat enemies like hatred. Anyone else is just fighting dead bodies.
Suffering also has a good quality. Sadness stops us from feeling superior. We feel compassion for those in the cycle of rebirth. We avoid harmful deeds and enjoy good deeds.
Things like bile cause great suffering, but we do not get angry at them. So why get angry at a being with a mind? They are also pushed by circumstances.
For example, sickness happens even when we do not want it. In the same way, troubling emotions rise up with force even when we do not want them.
People get angry over little things without even thinking, "I will get angry." In the same way, anger just happens without us deciding to make it.
Every single fault and all kinds of harmful deeds happen because of circumstances. They do not have independence.
Even those circumstances that come together do not think, "I will make this happen." And the thing they make does not think, "I am being made."
Whatever people call Primal Matter, and whatever people call the self, do not decide to exist. They do not think, "I will come to be."
If it does not exist before it begins, what could wish to exist? Because it would always be busy with things we sense, it could never stop.
If that self is lasting forever, it clearly does nothing, just like space. Even if it meets other circumstances, what can change something that never changes?
If something stays exactly the same while it acts, what did the action do to it? What connection could there be? How could anyone say, "This is its action"?
So, everything is controlled by other forces. Because of this power, everything is powerless. Knowing this, I will not get angry at any things. They are just like magic illusions.
Someone might ask, "What can stop what? Even stopping things makes no sense!" But because things depend on each other, it does make sense. It is not wrong to wish for sufferings to be cut away.
Therefore, whether it is an enemy or a friend, if I see them doing something wrong, I will think, "This has come from these circumstances." I will think this way and stay at ease.
If things happened just by their own choice, suffering would never happen to anyone. Since no one wants suffering, it would never arise for any beings with a body.
Through carelessness, people even hurt themselves with thorns and other things. To get women and other things they want, they get very worked up and start going without food.
Some people hang themselves or jump off cliffs. They eat poison and bad food. They bring harm to themselves through a way of acting that builds no store of goodness.
When people are controlled by a troubling emotion, they might even kill themselves. If they can hurt themselves like this, how could they not hurt others?
A troubling emotion can make people do terrible things like killing themselves. If compassion does not even arise for them, what sense is there in anger?
If hurting others is just the nature of a childish person, it is wrong to feel anger toward them. That would be like being mad at fire because its nature is to burn.

Or what if this bad behavior is only temporary, and the nature of living beings is gentle? Even then, it is wrong to feel anger. That would be like being mad at the sky just because smoke rises in it.
Someone might hit me with a stick. If I feel anger at the person swinging it, I must remember they are driven by hatred. It makes more sense to feel anger at hatred itself.
In the past, I hurt living beings like this. Because I harmed living beings, it is only right that I get hurt now.
His weapon and my body are both causes of suffering. He brought the weapon, and I brought my body. So who should get my anger?
This body is like a painful sore shaped like a person. It is full of suffering and hurts to touch. Blinded by wanting, I held onto it. When it gets hurt, who should get my anger?
A childish person does not want suffering. But they still want the causes of suffering. When they are hurt by their own mistakes, why should they blame others?
Think of the hell guardians and the forest of sword leaves. My own actions made them appear. So who should get my anger?
Pushed by my own actions, people appear and hurt me. If doing this makes them go to hell, haven't I ruined them?
Because of them, I practice patience. This wipes away my many harmful deeds. But because of me, they go to the hells. They face long-lasting suffering there.
I am the one who harms them. They are the ones who help me. O wicked mind, why do you act in such a mistaken way? Why do you create anger?
If my intention has a good quality, I will not go to hell. But if I just protect myself, what will happen to them?
If I harm them back, they will not be safe. My good way of acting will get worse. Then my hard practice will be ruined.
The mind is not a being with a body. Because of this, no one can destroy it anywhere. But by holding on tightly to the body, the body is hurt by sufferings.
Disrespect, harsh words, and unpleasant talk do not harm the body. O mind, why do you feel such strong anger?

I might say, "By staying alive through gain, I will wipe out harmful deeds and build a store of goodness." But if I feel anger to get that gain, won't my store of goodness run out? Won't more harmful deeds happen?
If the very reason I live is destroyed, what is the point of living? What good is a life that only does harmful deeds?
You might say, "I feel anger at people who say mean things, because they ruin living beings." But people say mean things about others too. Why do you not feel anger about that?
A lack of faith depends on other people. If you have patience for people without faith, why not have patience for people who speak badly? Their bad words just depend on a troubling emotion.
Some people insult and destroy statues, shrines, and the holy teachings. Even then, it is wrong for me to feel hatred. The Buddhas and others cannot be harmed by this.
Some people harm my teachers, relatives, and friends. But just like before, I see that this harm only comes from circumstances. Seeing this, I should stop my anger.
If other people being upset with me will not destroy me in this life or another life, why do I dislike it?
If I dislike this because it puts something in the way of my gain, my gain will just be left behind here. But my harmful deeds will stay firmly with me.
It is better to die today than to live a long time through a wrong way to earn a living. Even if I stay alive for a long time, the suffering of death is exactly the same.
Think of a person who wakes up after enjoying happiness in a dream for a hundred years. Think of another person who wakes up after enjoying happiness for just one moment.
For both of the people who wake up, that happiness does not return. For both a long life and a short life, it is exactly the same at the time of death.
Even if I get a lot of gain and enjoy happiness for a long time, I will leave naked and empty-handed. I will be just like someone robbed by a thief.
Both a being with a mind and a thing without a mind can hurt a being with a body. Why do we only blame the being with a mind? Therefore, practice patience when you are harmed.
Some people do bad things because of confusion. Others react with anger because of confusion. Which of them is without fault? And which one is to blame?
Why did I do the past action that makes others harm me? If everything comes from action, why should I be angry about this?
Seeing this, I must try my best to build my store of goodness. I will do this so that everyone can have a loving mind for one another.
Imagine a fire spreading from one burning house to another. If the fire catches on straw or things like that, people pull the straw out and throw it away.
In the same way, the fire of hatred spreads to whatever the mind has clinging to. To stop my store of goodness from burning, I must throw that clinging away right now.
If a person about to be killed loses a hand but goes free, isn't that good? If human suffering frees someone from hell, isn't that a good thing?
If I cannot bear even this much suffering right now, why do I not stop my anger? Anger is the cause of suffering in hell.
Because of my desire for pleasure, I have suffered burning in hell thousands of times. Yet I have not achieved my own good or the good of others.
This is not so harmful, and it will achieve great things. I should only be glad about suffering that takes away the harm from beings.
If others find joy by praising those who have good qualities, O my mind, why don't you praise them and rejoice in that same way?
This happiness of rejoicing is a source of joy without any blame. It is allowed by people with good qualities. It is also the best way to bring others together.
The honor of praise and fame does not build my store of goodness. It does not give me a long life. It does not become my strength or health. It does not even make my body comfortable.
If I really knew my own good, what own good is there in that? If I only want my mind to feel happy, I must also rely on gambling and alcohol.
If I waste my wealth for the sake of fame, and even get myself killed, what is the use of mere words? Once I am dead, who will be made happy by them?
When a sandcastle falls down, children cry in despair. In the same way, when praise and fame fade away, my own mind acts just like a child.
First of all, a sound has no mind. It cannot possibly mean to praise me. People might say that others are pleased with me. Is that a reason to feel joy?
Whether someone is pleased with another person or with me, how does their joy help me? That joy and happiness belong only to them. I do not get a share of it.
The happiness you feel from rejoicing is a source of joy without any blame. A person with good qualities allows it. It is also the best way to bring others together.
Whether someone gets a gift, or it stays in the giver's house, you do not have it either way. So what does it matter if it is given or not?
Why do you throw away your store of goodness, your faith, or your own good qualities? You let go of what brings you gains. Tell me, why are you not angry at yourself?
You feel no sorrow for the harmful deeds you yourself have done. On top of that, do you want to compete with others who have built up a store of goodness? The Second Fascicle.
Even if an enemy is unhappy, what is there for you to be glad about? Your wishing alone will not cause him any harm.
Even if your wishes make that suffering happen, what is there for you to be glad about? If you say, 'I will be satisfied,' what could ruin you more than that?
The fisherman of troubling emotions throws a terrible hook that is hard to bear. If I am caught by it, the hell guardians will certainly boil me in the cauldrons of hell.
You might think, "Paying them will make them happy." If you do not want them to be happy, you might not pay their wages. That will ruin this life and the next.
When people praise your own good qualities, you want others to be happy too. When they praise the good qualities of others, you do not even want happiness for yourself.
You want happiness for all living beings. You showed this by giving rise to the awakening mind for awakening. If living beings find happiness themselves, why do you get angry at that?
You want living beings to achieve becoming a Buddha. You want the three worlds to honor them. When you see them receive just a little respect, why does that upset you?
Imagine someone you must take care of and give things to. If that relative finds a way to support themselves, do you get angry instead of being glad?
If you do not want this for beings, who will want awakening for them? If someone gets angry at another person's success, where is their awakening mind?
If I am happy because they are happy, I should feel this way toward everyone. Why am I not happy when they are happy for someone else?
Feeling joy just because I think I am praised makes no sense. It is nothing but the behavior of a child.
Praise and similar things distract me. They destroy my weariness with the cycle of rebirth. They cause jealousy toward those with good qualities. They also destroy excellence.
Some people are around just to destroy my praise. Are they not protecting me from falling into an unhappy realm?
Since I seek freedom, I do not need the chains of gain and honor. These people give me freedom from being tied up. How could I be angry with them?
When I wish to step into suffering, these people become a door that keeps me out. They act like a blessing of the Buddha. How could I be angry with them?
I might think someone is blocking my store of goodness, but it is not right to be angry even at them. Since there is no hard practice equal to patience, should I not stay patient?
If my own faults stop me from practicing patience with this, I am the one making a block. The cause of a store of goodness is right in front of me.
If one thing cannot happen without another, and it happens when the other is there, then that is its cause. How can it be called a block?
A beggar arriving at the right time is not a block to giving. Someone who helps you in becoming a monk or nun cannot be called a block to becoming a monk or nun.
There are many beggars in the world, but people who cause harm are rare. If I do not hurt others, no one will hurt me.
Therefore, an enemy is like a treasure that appears in the house without any hard work. Since they are a helper in the way of acting for awakening, I should be happy with my enemy.
Patience is created by both my enemies and me. So, I should offer the result of patience to them first. This is because they are the cause of patience.
Someone might say I should not honor my enemy, because they do not intend to help me practice patience. If so, why do we honor the holy teachings? They are also a good cause that helps us succeed.
Someone might say I should not honor my enemy because they actually want to harm me. But if they tried to help me like a kind doctor, how could I ever learn patience?
Therefore, patience only arises because of a very hateful mind. Since they are the exact cause of patience, they deserve to be honored just like the holy teachings.
Because of this, the Sage taught about the field of living beings and the field of the Victorious Ones. By making them happy, many have reached the perfection of excellence.
Living beings and the Victorious Ones both help us achieve the qualities of a Buddha. Just as we respect the Victorious Ones, why do we not respect living beings too?
They do not have the exact same intention. But they are alike because of the result. Just like the Buddhas, living beings also have good qualities. That is why they are equal.
Making an offering to someone with a loving mind shows the greatness of living beings. The store of goodness that comes from having faith in the Buddhas shows the greatness of the Buddhas.

Living beings have a part in helping me gain every quality of a Buddha. That is why living beings and the Buddhas are seen as equal. But no one is truly equal to the Buddhas. They have an endless ocean of good qualities.
If even a tiny part of a supreme good quality appears in someone, I should honor them. Even giving them the three realms as a gift would be too little.
A small part of the greatest qualities of a Buddha grows in living beings. Because they have this small part, it is right to treat living beings as worthy of gifts.
The Buddhas are true friends who never trick me. They help me in ways I cannot measure. How could I ever pay them back? The only way is by making living beings happy.

They give up their bodies for these people. They even enter the Avichi hell for them. Helping these people is a way to pay them back. So, even if people cause me great harm, I should treat them all with complete goodness.
Even my own lords do not care about their own bodies to help these people. How could a fool like me act with pride toward them and not act as a servant?
The Sages are happy when these people are happy. They are upset when these people are hurt. By bringing them joy, I please all the Sages. By harming them, I harm the Sages.
If someone's body is completely on fire, nothing nice can make them happy. In the same way, when living beings are hurt, there is no way to please those with great compassion.
I have caused harm to beings. This has upset all those with great compassion. Today, I own up to each harmful deed. I pray the Sages forgive me for upsetting them.

To please the Thus-Gone Ones, I will be a servant to the world from today onward. Many beings might kick my head. They might even kill me. I will not fight back. May the Protectors of the World be pleased!

Those who have the nature of compassion have made all these beings into themselves. I have no doubt about this. The ones we see as living beings are those Protectors themselves. Why do I not respect them?
This alone is what pleases the Thus-Gone Ones. This alone perfectly achieves my own good. This alone takes away the suffering of the world. Therefore, I will always practice this alone.
For example, imagine one of a king's men hurts many people. People who look ahead do not hurt him back, even if they can.
This is because he is not alone. The king's power is his power. In the same way, I should never look down on a weak person who causes harm.
This is because the hell guardians and the compassionate ones are his forces. Therefore, just as subjects please a fierce king, I should please living beings.
Even if a king gets angry, could he cause that harm of hell? That is what we will suffer if we displease living beings.
What is joyful effort? It is taking delight in a good deed. Now I will explain its opposite. The opposite is laziness, clinging to what is bad, and discouragement, which is looking down on oneself.
Laziness comes from enjoying the pleasure of idleness. It grows from the wanting that comes with sleep. It also happens when you do not feel tired of the suffering in the cycle of rebirth.
You are chased by the hunter of troubling emotions. You are caught in the net of birth. You have walked into the mouth of the Lord of Death. How do you still not know this?
Have you not seen your own friends and family dying one by one? Yet you just keep sleeping. You are like a buffalo standing right next to its butcher.
All the paths are blocked. The Lord of Death is watching you. How can you enjoy eating? How can you enjoy sleeping like this?
You will die very quickly. Until then, you should gather stored-up goodness. Even if you give up laziness at the very end, what can you do when it is too late?
Even if I make a king happy, he cannot give me the state of a Buddha. I can only get that by making living beings happy.
Leave aside becoming a Buddha in the future by making living beings happy. Why do I not see that great glory, fame, and happiness will come to me in this very life?
While in the cycle of rebirth, patience brings me beauty, health, and fame. I will also get a very long life and the great happiness of a king of the whole world.
This is the sixth chapter from Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero. It is called Patience.
Chapter Seven: Teaching Joyful Effort
Now that I have patience, I must start joyful effort. Awakening depends on this hard work. Just as nothing moves without the wind, a store of goodness does not grow without joyful effort.
I will think, "I haven't finished this. I just started that. This is only half done." Then the Lord of Death will suddenly arrive. I will think, "Oh no, I am ruined!"
My relatives will lose all hope. Their eyes will be red and puffy from crying. Tears will run down their faces. Then I will look into the faces of the messengers of Yama.
Remembering my own harmful deeds will torment me. I will hear the sounds of hell. I will be so terrified that I soil myself. When my mind gets confused, what will I do?
In this life, you flip around in fear like a live fish out of water. Since you have done harmful deeds, there is no need to mention the unbearable sufferings of hell!
When hot water touches you, your soft skin burns badly. You have done actions that lead to hell. Why are you just relaxing like this?
You want the result without trying hard. You are fragile and face many harms. Death is grabbing you, yet you act like a god. Oh no, you are destroyed by sufferings!
Use the boat of a human body to cross the great river of suffering! This boat will be hard to find later. So do not be foolish and sleep right now!
The holy teachings are an endless cause of joy. Why have you left their great joy behind? Why do you enjoy distraction by the causes of suffering, along with restlessness and the like?
Let go of discouragement. Gather your force with wholehearted commitment and mastery of oneself. Practice seeing self and others as equal! Practice swapping self and others!
Do not fall into discouragement by thinking, "How could I ever reach awakening?" The Thus-Gone One is the Speaker of Truth, and he has spoken this truth:
Think of flies, mosquitoes, bees, and worms. Even they can build up the power of joyful effort. If they do, they will reach the highest awakening, which is very hard to achieve.
I have been born as a human being. I know what is helpful and what is harmful. If I do not give up the way of acting for awakening, why should I not reach awakening?
I might think, "I am afraid to give away my arms and legs." But this fear is just confusion. I am not thinking about what is truly hard and what is easy.
For countless millions of great ages, I will be cut many times. I will be pierced, burned, and split apart. Even so, I will not reach awakening.
The suffering of reaching awakening has a limit. It is just like the pain of cutting the body open. You do it to pull out a splinter that is destroying you from the inside.
All doctors cure sickness by causing some discomfort with their treatments. Therefore, to destroy many sufferings, I should put up with a little discomfort.
The Greatest Doctor does not use normal treatments like these. He uses a very gentle method. With it, he cures countless great diseases.
At first, the Guide starts us off with giving vegetables and things like that. Once we get used to that, we can slowly learn to give away even our own flesh.
When I think of my own body as being like simple vegetables, giving away my flesh is no longer hard. What difficulty is there in that?
If I give up every harmful deed, I will have no suffering. If I am a wise person, I will not be unhappy. It is wrong thinking and harmful deeds that hurt the mind and body.
A store of goodness puts the body at ease. Being a wise person puts the mind at ease. Even while staying in the cycle of rebirth for the good of others, why would a compassionate one get tired?
The power of the awakening mind wipes out every past harmful deed. It also gathers an ocean of stored goodness. Because of this, the bodhisattva is greater than the Hearers.
So climb onto the horse of the awakening mind! It takes away all tiredness. As you ride from happiness to happiness, what smart person would ever fall into discouragement?

To help living beings, we need four kinds of strength. These are a strong wish, steadiness, joy, and letting go. A strong wish grows from the fear of suffering and from thinking about the benefits of that wish.

I must leave the opposite behind. I should try hard to grow my joyful effort. I will do this through a strong wish, pride, joy, and letting go. I will also use the power of wholehearted commitment and mastery.
I must destroy the countless faults of myself and others. It would take an ocean of great ages to end each and every fault.
I do not see even a tiny bit of effort in myself to end those faults. I am a place of endless suffering. Why does my heart not burst?
I must build up many good qualities in myself and others. I must practice each and every good quality for an ocean of great ages.
But I have never practiced even a tiny part of a good quality. I somehow found this life. It is amazing that I have made it meaningless.
I have not made offerings to the Blessed One. I have not shared the joy of a great festival. I have not served the teachings. I have not fulfilled the wishes of the poor.

Because of my good deeds, I will become a child of the Well-Gone One. I will sit in front of the Victorious One. I will live inside a huge, cool, sweet-smelling lotus. The sweet words of the Victorious One will feed my bright glow. The light of the Sage will open my lotus, and I will have a perfect body.

By doing many bad deeds, I will fall onto the intensely burning iron ground. The helpers of Yama will cause me great pain by tearing off all my skin. They will pour melted, hot copper over my body. Blazing swords and short spears will pierce me, cutting my flesh into a hundred pieces.
Because of this, I should really want to do good deeds. I must practice them with great respect. Using the method of Vajradhvaja, once I begin, I should grow my pride.
First, I should check my resources. Then I must decide to start or not to start. It is best not to begin at all. But once I begin, I should not turn back.

If I get used to turning back, it will happen in another life too. My harmful deeds and suffering will increase. Any new action and its results will become weak. Then that action will not get finished either.
I should build my pride in three things: my action, my troubling emotions, and my ability. Thinking, "I will do this alone," is called pride in action.
If I have not given freedom from fear to frightened people, and I have not given happiness to sad people, then my birth only caused my mother pain and suffering.
Because I did not have a strong wish for the teachings in the past, and still do not have it now, I have ended up so poor. Who would ever give up a strong wish for the teachings?
The Sage has said that a strong wish is the root of every kind of good deed. The root of that strong wish is always meditating on the result that ripens.
Suffering and unhappiness, many kinds of fears, and losing what we want all come from doing harmful deeds.
By doing a good deed planned in your mind, wherever you go, your store of goodness will bring you honor and the gifts of its results.
People who do harmful deeds might want happiness. But wherever they go, those harmful deeds will destroy them with the weapons of suffering.
This world has no power because of troubling emotions. It cannot achieve its own good. Other beings are not able to help themselves like I can. So, I will do this work.
If others are doing lesser things, how can I just sit and do nothing? I do not act out of pride. For me, it is best to be without pride.
When a crow finds a dead snake, it acts like a giant sky bird. If I am weak, even a small fall will hurt me.
If someone feels sad and gives up their effort, can they ever escape their hardships? By building up pride and effort, you become hard to defeat even by great downfalls.
Therefore, I must conquer falls with a strong mind. If a fall defeats me, my wish to conquer the three realms will just be a joke.
I will conquer everything, and no one will conquer me. I am a child of the Victorious Lion. I will stay in this pride.

Anyone who is beaten by pride has a troubling emotion. They do not have true pride. Someone with true pride does not fall under the enemy's power. The others fall under the power of the enemy called pride.
People puffed up by the troubling emotion of pride are led by pride to an unhappy realm. Their human joy is ruined, and they become slaves who eat other people's food.
They are foolish, ugly, and weak. People look down on them everywhere. If a person of hard practice is puffed up with pride and counted among the proud, tell me, what are the lowest people like?

Whoever holds onto pride to beat the enemy called pride is truly proud. They are a winning hero. Whoever destroys the strong enemy called pride perfects the result of winning for wandering beings, just as they wish.
