If I live right in the middle of troubling emotions, I will stay strong in a thousand ways. I will be like a lion among foxes. I will not be hurt by the crowd of troubling emotions.
When great danger comes, a person naturally protects their eyes. In the same way, even if danger comes, I will not fall under the power of troubling emotions.
If someone drops a sword in battle, they quickly pick it up out of fear. If I drop my weapon of keeping in mind, I must quickly pick it up too. I must remember the fears of hell.
Poison uses the blood to spread all through the body. In the same way, if a fault finds a chance, it will spread all through the mind.
Imagine carrying a bowl full of oil while someone with a sword stands nearby. You would fear death if you spilled it. A strict practitioner must be just as focused.
If a snake crawled into your lap, you would jump up right away. In the same way, if sleep and sluggishness come, I must quickly push them away.
Every time a fault happens, I will scold myself. I will think about it for a long time. I will say, "I must make sure this never happens to me again."
I should ask myself, "How can keeping in mind become a habit in these situations?" For this reason, I should seek out the right company or do the right actions.
Just as I want the happiness that comes from playing a game, I should love whatever action I need to do. I should find joy in it and never get tired of it.
Even if I do something just to get happiness, I am not sure if happiness will really come. But if the action itself becomes happiness, how could I have happiness without doing it?
We never get enough of a desire for pleasure, which is like licking honey from a razor's edge. So how could I ever get enough of a store of goodness? Its ripening is happiness and peace.
Therefore, to finish my task, I should dive right into the action. I should be like a hot elephant in the midday sun that finds a cool lake and plunges right in.
If my strength starts to fade, I should set the action aside so I can finish it later. Once a task is completely done, I should leave it behind, eager to start the next one.
Just like a brave warrior fighting enemies with swords on a battlefield, I must dodge the weapons of the troubling emotions. Then I must strike hard to destroy those enemy troubling emotions.
Before I act, I want to be ready for anything. By remembering the teachings on carefulness, I should make myself jump up lightly.
Just as the wind blows a piece of cotton around, I should let eagerness guide me. That is how I will succeed.
From Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero, this is the seventh chapter, called Joyful Effort.
Chapter Eight: Calm Focus
Now that I have grown my joyful effort, I should place my mind in deep focus. A person whose mind is totally distracted is caught between the fangs of troubling emotions.
By keeping my body and mind in solitude, a wandering mind will not happen. Therefore, I should leave the world behind and completely drop every restless thought.
We do not leave the world behind because of clinging. We are stuck wanting gain and other things. So, a wise person should completely let go of these things and think like this.
Clear seeing joined with calm abiding completely destroys troubling emotions. Knowing this, I should first look for calm abiding. I can reach it by finding joy in freedom from clinging to the world.
Why would a being who is not lasting feel true clinging for someone else who is not lasting? Because of this, they will not see their loved ones for thousands of lifetimes.
If we do not see them, we feel no joy, and the mind does not rest as a settled mind. Even when we do see them, we are never satisfied. We are still hurt by wanting, just as before.
If we become attached to living beings, what is truly real is completely hidden. The weary mind is also destroyed. In the end, we will be hurt by sorrow.
By just thinking about them, this life will pass away with no meaning. Because of friends who are not lasting, even the eternal teachings will be destroyed.
I will stay far away from a foolish person. If we meet, I will be friendly and make them happy. But I will not get too close. I will just act like an ordinary person.

A bee just takes nectar from a flower and flies away. In the same way, I will only take what helps me practice the teachings. I will stay slightly apart from everyone, as if I had never met them before.
I might think that I have much gain and honor, and that many people like me. If I hold onto that puffed-up feeling, fear will come to me after I die.
Therefore, my confused mind might hold tightly to many things. But all those things will add up together. They will grow a thousand times bigger and turn into suffering.
Therefore, a wise person should avoid clinging, because fear comes from clinging. All these things will naturally be left behind anyway. I must stay strong and understand this completely.
I might gather a lot of gain, fame, and a good name. But even with all that gain and fame, I have no idea where I will go after I die.
If I share the same path as a childish person, I will certainly go to an unhappy realm. If they lead me away from the noble path, what is the use of relying on a childish person?
They become friends in an instant. Then they become enemies just as fast. They get mad even at happy things. An ordinary person is very hard to please.
If I say helpful things, they become angry. They also stop me from doing helpful things. If I do not listen to them, their anger will make them fall into an unhappy realm.

They feel jealousy toward those above them. They compete with their equals. They show pride toward those below them, and act stuck-up when praised. If someone speaks to them unkindly, they feel anger. When will I ever get any benefit from a foolish person?

If I spend time with a childish person, I will hear them praising oneself and putting others down. They will talk happily about the cycle of rebirth. Every kind of bad deed will surely come from this.
If we rely on each other like this, we will only ruin ourselves. They will not do me any good. And I will not do them any good either.
If there are others who speak badly of me, why should praise make me glad? If there are others who praise me, why should I be sad when people speak badly of me?

Living beings have many different strong wishes. If even the Victorious Ones cannot please them all, how could an ordinary person like me do it? Therefore, I will let go of my thoughts about the world.
Living beings say bad things about people without gains. They also say mean things about people with gains. They are naturally hard to be around. How could they ever bring me joy?
A childish person is never happy unless they get something for themselves. Because of this, the Thus-Gone Ones have said that no childish person is a friend.
In the forest, deer, birds, and trees do not say mean things. When will I live with them? Their company is so pleasant.
I will make my home in a cave, an empty temple, or at the foot of a tree. When will I stop looking back and become entirely free from clinging?
When will I live in wide, open places that no one calls "mine"? When will I live there freely, without holding on to anything?
When will I live without fear? I will own just an alms bowl and a few small things. I will wear clothes that no one wants, and I will not even hide this body.
When will I go to a place of the dead? When will I treat my own body and the skeletons of others as exactly the same? Both are meant to pass away.
One day, even this very body of mine will change. It will smell so bad that not even foxes will come near it.
This body came to be as one whole thing. But the flesh and bones that were born together will break down and separate. If my own body falls apart, why even mention other friends?
I was born alone, and I will die alone. No one else can take a share of my suffering. So what is the use of friends who only get in the way?
People traveling on a road find a place to stay. In the same way, those on the path of life find a place to be born.
While the world grieves all around, go to the forest! Do this before four men carry your body away.
This body lives all alone, making no friends and no enemies. Since I act like I am already dead, no one will feel sorrow when I die.
No one stays nearby to cause the harm of sorrow. Because of this, no one will distract me from remembering the Buddha and other things.
Therefore, I will live all alone in beautiful, joyful forests that are free from hardship. These forests calm all distractions.
I will let go of all other thoughts. I will focus only on my own mind. I will work hard at settling the mind and taming it.
In this world and the next, desire for pleasure brings ruin. Here, it leads to being killed, tied up, and hurt. In the next life, it brings about the hells.
In the past, you sent many messengers to win their love. You did not hesitate to do harmful deeds or ruin your good name for them.
You even put yourself in danger and spent all your wealth for them. You thought that hugging them would make you perfectly happy.
But those very people are nothing but skeletons! They have no independence and no self. Why do you desire them and hold on so tightly? Why do you not go to freedom from sorrow?
When you first lifted the cloth with effort, that face looked down shyly. Whether you had seen it before or not, that face was covered.
That face became a troubling emotion for you. Now it is right out in the open. Seeing it uncovered by vultures, why do you run away from it now?
If you are not attached to filth, why do you hug another person? They are a cage of bones tied together. They are covered with the mud of flesh.
You are full of filth yourself. You carry it around all the time. Yet you still want other bags of filth. You desire them out of greed for filth.
You say, 'I love this flesh.' You want to touch and look at it. But how can you desire this flesh? It is naturally without a mind.
The mind you want cannot be seen or touched. The part you can touch is not awareness. So what is the point of that useless hug?
Another person's body has the nature of filth. It is not surprising if you do not realize this. But you yourself are filth itself. It is a great wonder that you do not realize that!
You leave behind a fresh lotus opened by the bright sun. Your mind is attached to filth. Why do you find joy in a cage of filth?
Even when others just looked at it with their eyes, you guarded it completely. While it is being eaten by them, why do you not guard it, you stingy person?
When you see this heap of flesh, vultures and others will eat it. Why do you honor the food of others with flower garlands, sandalwood, and ornaments?
When you see a simple skeleton, you are terrified even if it does not move. Why are you not afraid when something moves it, like a corpse that walks?
Body waste and spit are both made from the exact same food. Out of these two, you dislike the body waste. So why do you like the spit?
A person full of desire does not enjoy a soft cotton pillow. They say, "It does not leak a bad smell." They are confused about what is unclean.
If you feel clinging to this even when it is covered, why do you not want it when it is uncovered? If you have no need for that, why do you hug it when it is covered?
If you refuse to touch a patch of ground smeared with filth, how can you want to touch the body it came from?
If you do not like filth, why do you hold someone in your lap who grew from an unclean field and was made by that seed?
You do not want even a tiny worm born in filth. Yet you want a body that is full of filth and born from filth.
You do not even hate your own filth. But out of greed for filth, you also desire another bag of filth.
Think of nice things like camphor, cooked rice, or vegetables. Once you put them in your mouth and spit them out, they make the ground foul.
If you doubt this filth even when it is plain to see, look at the bodies left in the place of the dead. Look at that other filth too.
If you feel sick seeing only skeletons in the place of the dead, why do you like the village? The village is also a place of the dead. It is filled with moving skeletons.
Even things that are impure cost a price to get. Working for that goal just makes you tired. It also brings harm in hell and other places.
A child cannot gather wealth. When they grow up, what happiness is there in this? If you spend your whole life gathering wealth, you will get old. What can you do then with your desire for pleasure?
An unhappy person full of desire works all day and gets completely tired out. They come home, and their tired bodies sleep like dead bodies.
Some people travel to other places and experience the suffering of going far away. They long to see their wives and children. But they do not see them for years.

Some people are completely confused. They want to help themselves, so they even sell themselves for a goal. But they do not get what they want. They are just blown around by the wind of other people's meaningless work.
Some people sell their own bodies. They have no power and must work for others. When their wives have babies, it happens just anywhere. It might be at the foot of a tree or out in the wild.

Fools are tricked by desire for pleasure. They want to survive and think, "I will make a living." They go into battle even though they fear losing their lives. They become servants just to make a profit.
Some people full of desire have their bodies cut apart. Some are stuck on the sharp points of stakes. Some are pierced by short spears. Some are even seen being burned.

Gathering, guarding, and losing wealth brings pain. You should know that wealth causes endless ruin. People get distracted by clinging to wealth. Then they have no chance to be free from the suffering of life.
For people full of desire, these are some of the many drawbacks. The enjoyment they get is very small. They are like animals pulling a cart. The animals only get to eat a few bites of grass.

People destroy this free and fortunate life, which is so hard to find. They do this just for a tiny bit of enjoyment. Even animals can easily get that small pleasure. These people are hurt by their own actions.
If the skin is peeled away from it, you will feel great fear. Since you know this, how can you feel joy for that same thing again?
The smell rubbed on the body is just sandalwood and things like that. It is nothing else. Because of that smell of another, why do you have clinging to another?
If it naturally smells bad, isn't it better to have no clinging to it? Why do people in the world who crave for no reason rub sweet smells on it?
But if the sweet smell is sandalwood, what actually comes from the body here? Because of the smell of another, why do you have clinging to another?
If it has long hair and nails, dirty yellow teeth, and the smell of mud, the nature of the body is truly scary when naked.
Why do you work so hard to care for it, like a weapon that hurts you? Through the efforts of people confused about the self, this earth is completely stirred up by madmen.
If you still doubt this is unclean, even when it is easy to see, look at the bodies left in the place of the dead. Look at those other unclean things, too.
Some people sell their own bodies. They have no power and must work for others. When their wives have babies, it happens just anywhere. It might be at the foot of a tree or out in the wild.
Sometimes a person full of desire gets their body cut apart. Some are stuck on the sharp points of stakes. Short spears pierce others. You can even see some being burned.
A person full of desire faces these and many other drawbacks. Their enjoyment is very small. They are just like animals pulling a cart. Those animals only eat a few mouthfuls of grass.
A desire for pleasure will certainly fade away. It causes a person to fall into hell and other bad places. We go through so much tiring hardship all the time for something that is not even great.
A tiny fraction of that hardship could bring us to the state of a Buddha. A person full of desire goes through suffering worse than the way of acting for awakening. Yet they get no awakening at all.
Think about the suffering in hell caused by a desire for pleasure. Weapons, poison, fire, steep cliffs, and enemies are not nearly as bad. They cannot even be used as examples.
Once you grow tired of desire, you should feel joy for solitude. Go into the peaceful forests. They are completely empty of arguments and troubling emotions.

Lucky people rest in lovely places made of wide stone slabs. They are cooled by moonlight and sandalwood. A quiet, peaceful forest breeze blows on them. They walk around and think about how to help others.

They stay in empty houses, under trees, and in caves. They stay wherever they want for as long as they like. They leave behind the suffering of owning and guarding things. They live a carefree life without depending on anything.
If I act on my own without clinging, I am not tied to anyone at all. The joy of being happy with enough is hard even for Indra to find.
By thinking about these things, I see the good qualities of solitude. When my busy thinking is completely calm, I should meditate on the awakening mind.
First, I should try hard to meditate on seeing self and others as equal. Since everyone is equal in happiness and suffering, I should protect everyone just like myself.

A body has many parts, like hands, but it is protected as one whole body. In the same way, there are many different beings with their own happiness and suffering. But they are all one in wanting happiness just like me.
My suffering does not hurt the bodies of others. Even so, that suffering is mine. It is unbearable because of holding on tightly to a self.
In the same way, the suffering of others does not fall on me. Even so, that suffering is mine. It is hard to bear because of holding on tightly to a self.
I should take away the suffering of others. It is suffering, just like my own suffering. I should help other living beings. They are like my very own body.
Other people want happiness just as much as I do. We are exactly the same. So why do I only work for my own happiness?
Other people hate suffering just as much as I do. We are exactly the same. So why do I protect myself and not others?
If I do not protect others because their suffering does not hurt me, why do I protect myself from future suffering? That future suffering does not hurt me right now.
Thinking that I will experience it is false. The person who dies is someone else, and the person who is born is also someone else.
If everyone only has to protect themselves from their own suffering, think about the foot. The suffering of the foot is not the hand's suffering. So why does the hand protect the foot?
You might say, "Even if it makes no sense, we act by holding on to a self." But anything that makes no sense about yourself and others should be given up as best as you can.
A continuing stream and a collection of parts are not real things. They are just words, like a necklace or an army. Since no one truly owns suffering, who is there to control it?
Suffering has no owner. Because of this, everyone is exactly the same. Because it is suffering, it must be cleared away. What is the point of making rules about who to help?
Someone might ask, "Why should we stop the suffering of everyone?" There is no room to argue. If we stop it, we must stop all of it. If not, then I must suffer just like any other living being.
Someone might ask, "Since compassion brings so much suffering, why force yourself to feel it?" But think about the suffering of all beings. Compared to that, how is the suffering of compassion great?
If facing one single suffering removes many other sufferings, a kind person should gladly accept it. They should be willing to bring about that suffering for themselves and others.
The Protector Avalokiteshvara felt great compassion. He wanted to take away the fear that beings feel in crowds. So, he put a blessing on his own name.
I should not give up when things are hard. The power of getting used to things changes us. You might once be scared to even hear someone's name. But later, you might feel no joy without them.
Do you want to quickly protect yourself and others? Then you should practice the exchange of self and others. This is the greatest secret.
Through clinging to this body of mine, I feel afraid of even small things. Since this body creates so much fear, who would not hate it like an enemy?
People want to cure their body's hunger and thirst. To do this, they kill birds, fish, and wild animals. They even wait in hiding along the roads.
Some want money and respect so much that they even kill their own parents. They steal wealth from the Three Jewels. Because of this, they will burn in the Avichi hell.
In the same way, why don't I see other people's bodies as "me"? Thinking of my own body as "other" is not hard to do.
I should know that I have faults and that others are oceans of good qualities. I must meditate on completely letting go of holding on to a self, and taking up others instead.
We accept that hands and other parts belong to the body. In the same way, why don't we accept that beings with a body are parts of all beings?

By getting used to it, the thinking mind of self has grown toward this body with no separate self. In the same way, why shouldn't the thinking mind of self grow toward other living beings by getting used to it?
If it is like that, doing the good of others will not make me feel amazed or proud. This is just like eating food myself. I do not hope for a reward when I eat.
Therefore, just as I protect myself from even tiny unpleasant things, I should get used to having a protective mind and a mind of compassion toward all beings.
This is why Supushpachandra did not stop his own suffering. He knew the king would hurt him. He did this so the suffering of many would end.
When my continuing stream gets used to this, I will love calming the suffering of others. I will dive right into the Avichi hell to help them. I will dive in like a swan landing in a lotus pond.
When living beings are freed, there is an ocean of joy. Is that joy not enough? What is the use of wanting freedom just for myself?
So even when I work for the good of others, I am not proud or amazed. I only find joy in the good of others. I do not hope for a result that ripens for me.
I protect myself from even the smallest mean word. I should protect others in the exact same way. I must grow a mind of compassion like this.
I grew used to thinking of drops from others as my own body. Even though they are without a thing that is really me, I call them 'I'.
Why say more? A childish person acts only for their own good. The Sage acts for the good of others. Just look at the difference between them!
If I do not exchange my own happiness for the suffering of others, I will never reach the state of a Buddha. Even in the cycle of rebirth, I will find no happiness.
Leave the next life aside for a moment. If a servant does not do their work and a master pays no wages, nothing gets done. They will not even reach their goals in this life.
Out of confusion, I might cause suffering to others. This only brings me unbearable suffering. I throw away the perfect joy that brings happiness I can see and cannot see.
Think of all the harm, fear, and suffering in the world. If all of it comes from holding on to a self, what use is that great demon to me?
If I do not completely let go of the self, I cannot leave suffering behind. It is just like fire. If I do not let go of the fire, I cannot stop being burned.
What wise person would want, protect, and honor that body? Who would not see it as an enemy and dislike it?
"If I give this away, what will I use?" Thinking of my own good is the way of a demon. "If I use this, what will I give away?" Thinking of the good of others is the way of a god.
If I harm others for my own sake, I will suffer in hell. If I harm myself for the sake of others, I will gain all excellence.
If I only wish to be great, I will be reborn in an unhappy realm as someone low and foolish. If I shift that wish to others, I will gain a happy realm and respect.
If I use others for my own good, I will become a servant. If I use myself for the good of others, I will become a master.
Whatever happiness there is in the world comes from wishing for the happiness of others. Whatever suffering there is in the world comes from wishing for my own happiness.
So, I want to stop harm to myself. I want to stop the suffering of others. To do this, I should give myself to others. I should treat others as myself.
My mind, you must know this for sure. I am under the power of others. Now you must think only about what helps every living being. Do not think of anything else.
My eyes and other parts belong to others. It is wrong to use them for my own good. They are for the sake of others. It is wrong to use them to harm others.
Therefore, put every living being first. Look at whatever is on my body. Take it away, and use it to help others.
Pretend that you are someone lower. Pretend that others are you. Clear your mind of busy thinking. Then practice feeling jealousy, rivalry, and pride.
People honor that person, but not me. I did not get what they got. That person is praised, but people say bad things about me. They are happy, but I am in suffering.
I do all the hard work, while this person just stays in happiness. This person is great in the world, but people say I am low and without good qualities.
What is the use of having no good qualities? Everyone has good qualities. There are people who are better than this person. There are also people who I am better than.
Losing my good conduct, my belief, and other things is caused by strong troubling emotions. It is out of my control. I must be healed as much as possible, and I will even accept harm.
But if this person will not heal me, why does he look down on me? What use are his good qualities to me? He is the one who has those good qualities!
Standing in the jaws of cruel unhappy realms, this person has no compassion for beings. He is proud of his good qualities. He even wants to challenge wise persons.
When I look at someone equal to me, I want to make myself better than them. I will certainly get my gain and respect, even if I have to argue.
I will make sure my good qualities are clear to the whole world. And whatever good qualities this person has, I will make sure no one hears about them.
I will also hide my faults. I will be honored, but not this person. Today I will get great things. I will be respected, but not this person.
When this person is ruined, I will gladly watch for a long time. I will make all beings laugh at them. I will make everyone make fun of them.
People say that even this miserable person is competing with me. But is this person equal to me in learning or wisdom? Are they equal in looks, family, or wealth?
Hearing my good qualities announced to everyone like this, I will feel a thrilling joy. I will fully enjoy this happiness.
Even if this person gets something, if they do my work, I will give them just enough to live on. I will take what they got using my power.
I will make this one lose his happiness. I will harm him all the time. He has hurt me for hundreds of lifetimes in the cycle of rebirth.
O mind, you only wanted your own good. Countless great ages have passed. You worked until you were very tired, but you only got suffering.
You must truly work hard to help others. The words of the Sage are never wrong. Later you will see the good qualities of doing this.
If you had helped others in the past, you would not be stuck like this. You would surely have the perfect happiness of a Buddha.
You are used to taking as "I" the drops of seed and blood from others. In the same way, get used to doing this for everyone else.
Act like a spy for other people. Watch whatever appears on my body. Snatch those things away, and practice what is good for others.
"I am happy and others are unhappy. I am high and others are low. I do good things and others do not." Why do you not feel jealousy toward yourself?
Give up your own happiness. Take the suffering of others onto yourself. Always ask, "What is this self doing right now?" Look closely at your own faults.
If others make a mistake, treat it as your own fault. But if you make even a small mistake, confess it to many people.
Praise other people so much that you hide your own fame. Act like the lowest servant. Put yourself to work for everyone else.
This self is full of faults. Do not praise it just for having a tiny, temporary good quality. Make sure that no one at all knows about your good qualities.
In short, think of any harm you have ever done to others for your own sake. Now, for the sake of all living beings, let that harm fall upon yourself.
Do not let it grow strong, or it will become bossy. Keep it held back with shame and fear, just like a new bride.
Tell it, 'Do this! Stay like that! Do not act that way!' Bring it under control like this. If it breaks the rules, you must stop it.
Even when I tell you what to do, if you do not listen, my mind, I must defeat you. All faults come from you, so I have no other choice.
That past time when you ruined me is over. Now I see you. Where will you go? I will destroy all your feeling superior.
Throw away the thought, 'I still have my own good!' I have sold you to others. Do not be sad. Just give them your help.
If I fall into carelessness and do not give you to living beings, you will surely hand me over to the guards of hell.
You have handed me over to suffering again and again. I have hurt for a long time. I remember those grudges. Now I will destroy your thoughts about your own good.
If I wish to be happy, I should not delight in myself. If I wish to protect myself, I should always protect others.
The more this body is completely cared for, the more fragile it becomes.
Once it becomes weak like that, even the whole earth cannot fulfill its desires. Who else could give it what it wants?
Wanting impossible things brings troubling emotions and ruins good intentions. But when someone does not depend on anything, their excellence will never run out.
Therefore, I should not let the desires of the body grow. Not grabbing onto attractive things is an excellent thing.
So, without being attached, I will give up my body to help others. It has many faults. Still, I will keep it like a tool for doing good.
I have had enough of acting like a child! I will follow the wise. I will remember the teachings on carefulness. I will chase away sleep and dullness of mind.
To clear away the veil, I will turn my mind away from wrong paths. I will always rest by settling the mind on the perfect thing to focus on.
From Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero, the eighth chapter, called Calm Focus.
Chapter Nine: The Perfection of Wisdom
The Sage taught all these branches for the sake of wisdom. So, anyone who wants to stop suffering should grow wisdom.
In the end, it will just turn to ashes. It cannot move unless something else moves it. This form is dirty and hard to bear. Why do I keep grabbing hold of a self in this?
Whether it is alive or dead, what use is this machine to me? If it is no different from a lump of dirt, oh, why do I not get rid of my pride?
By taking care of the body, I have only built up useless suffering. What is the point of clinging and anger toward this thing that is just like wood?
It does not matter if I take good care of it, or if vultures eat it. Since it has no clinging and no hatred, why do I feel clinging toward it?
If the thing that gets angry at blame and happy at praise actually knows nothing at all, then who have I worked so hard for?
If I say that anyone who desires this body is my friend, then why do I not delight in everyone? After all, everyone desires their own body.
People believe in two truths. They are everyday truth and deepest truth. Deepest truth is beyond the reach of the thinking mind. The thinking mind is just everyday truth.
We see two kinds of worlds. There is the world of the meditation master and the world of ordinary people. The world of the meditation master proves the ordinary world wrong.

Even a meditation master has a different level of thinking mind. Higher masters prove the lower ones wrong. They use examples they both agree on. They do not question these examples because they just want a result.
A person of the world sees a thing and believes it is what is truly real. They do not see that it is like an illusion. Because of this, the meditation master argues with the world.
Seeing directly a shape and other things is just common usage. It is not a reliable way of knowing. It is false, just like the common usage that calls filth by the name of cleanness.
To guide the world, the Protector taught about a thing. But in reality, things are not lasting only a moment. Someone might say, "This goes against even everyday truth!"

Someone might say, "Since even a Buddha would be trapped in the world, what is the use of the way of acting for awakening?" I reply: As long as the unbroken flow of circumstances is not cut, even an illusion will not stop.
But when the unbroken flow of circumstances is cut, it does not happen even in everyday truth. Someone might ask, "When even the mistake does not exist, what will see the illusion?"
I reply, "When you say the illusion itself does not exist, then what is seen?" Someone might answer, "If something else exists in the way things really are, that way it appears is the mind itself."
If the mind itself is an illusion, then what is seen by what? Even the Protector of the world taught that the mind cannot see the mind.
Just as a sword blade cannot cut itself, the mind cannot see itself. Someone might say, "But a lamp lights itself up perfectly!"
A lamp does not need to be lit up, because darkness does not hide it. Someone might argue, "Unlike a clear crystal, a blue thing does not depend on anything else for its blueness."
There is no mistake in the everyday truth of a meditator. Compared to the world, they see the way things really are. Otherwise, when they see women as unclean, the world would prove them wrong.

Someone might ask, "How do we get a store of goodness from a Victorious One who is like an illusion?" It is just like getting it from someone who is really existing. They might also ask, "If living beings are like illusions, how are they born again after they die?"
As long as the circumstances come together, an illusion will appear for that long. Just because they have a long unbroken flow, how can a living being be truly existing?
Killing a person made by magic is not a harmful deed, because they have no mind. But when acting toward someone who has the mind of an illusion, a store of goodness and a harmful deed can happen.

Because things like sacred words do not have the power, the mind of an illusion does not appear. Because it comes from many different circumstances, that illusion itself comes in many different kinds.
There is no single circumstance anywhere that has the power to do everything. Someone might say, "If the deepest truth is freedom from sorrow, and the cycle of rebirth is everyday truth, then..."

Someone might say an illusion is not different from the mind. But they also say it is not exactly the same. If it is a real thing, how is it not different? If it is not different, it does not exist as a thing.

Someone might say an illusion is not true, but we still see it. They say the mind is the one who sees. They might argue the cycle of rebirth must be based on a real thing. Otherwise, it would just be like empty space.
But if a non-existent thing depends on a real thing, how could it do anything? Without anything outside it, your mind would have no companion. Your mind would become completely alone.
When the mind is free of any thing the mind takes in, everyone becomes a Thus-Gone One. Even if this were true, what is the good of it? What is the point of making up the idea of Mind Only?

Someone might ask: Even if you know things are like an illusion, how will that stop troubling emotions? Think of a magician who creates a woman made by illusion. Even the magician can still feel clinging toward her.
That magician has not let go of his deep habits of troubling emotions toward things to know. Because of this, when he sees her, his deep habit of emptiness is very weak.
Someone might say, "We see that some things depend on other things, and some do not." But something that is not blue cannot make itself blue.
When awareness knows a lamp, we can say, "The lamp is shining." But what knows the thinking mind so we can say, "The thinking mind itself is shining"?
If no one sees it at all, it means nothing to say whether it is shining or not. It is like talking about the beautiful pose of the daughter of a woman with no children.

Someone might ask, "If there is no awareness of itself, how can we have a memory of awareness?" A memory happens because it is connected to experiencing something else. It is like the poison of a rat.

Someone might say, "Because of a special circumstance, a person can see that the mind shines to itself." But using magic eye ointment lets you see a hidden vase. It does not let you see the eye ointment itself.
I am not denying the things you see, hear, and know. I only want to stop you from thinking things are truly real. That is the cause of suffering.

Someone might ask, "If we make offerings to someone without a mind, how will we get a result?" It is because the teachings say it is exactly the same whether the Buddha stays here or has passed into freedom from sorrow.
Whether in everyday truth or in the way things really are, this makes sense. The sacred text says a result comes from it. It brings a result just like giving to a real Buddha.
Someone might say, "Freedom comes from seeing the truths. Why do we need to see emptiness?" The sacred text says that without this path, there is no awakening.
Someone might ask, "If the Great Vehicle is not proven, how is your sacred text proven?" You might answer, "Because we both agree on it." But at first, it was not proven for you either.
Whatever circumstance makes you believe in your text is the same for the Great Vehicle. If a text is true just because two groups accept it, then the Vedas and other books would also be true.

Someone might say, "We reject the Great Vehicle because people argue about it." But you argue with a non-Buddhist about your sacred text. You also argue with other groups about other sacred texts. Since people argue about them, you would have to throw them all away.

If you keep getting used to the habit of emptiness, you will let go of the habit left in the mind by things. By getting used to thinking "there is nothing," you will later let go of that deep habit too.
When you say, "This thing does not exist," and you cannot find the thing you are looking for, what happens? How can a non-existent thing without a base stay in front of the thinking mind?
When a thing and a non-existent thing do not stay in front of the thinking mind, there is no other way it appears. At that time, by having no object of focus, there is complete calm.
A wish-fulfilling jewel and a wish-granting tree completely grant our hopes. In the same way, the form of the Victorious One appears to the one to be guided through the power of a wishing prayer.
For example, a shrine for the great sky bird might be built. Even a long time after the builder passes away, it still clears away poison and other harms.
In the same way, following the way of acting for awakening, the shrine of the Victorious One has been built. Even after the awakening hero passes away, it still achieves every goal.
If being a monk is the root of the teaching, even being a monk is hard to prove. For people whose minds are holding on to things, even freedom from sorrow is hard to reach.
If someone is set free just by giving up troubling emotion, they would be free right away. But even without troubling emotion, we still see the power of action in them.

Someone might say it is certain that, for now, the wanting that causes holding on does not exist. Even if that wanting is not troubled by troubling emotion, why would it not exist? It would be just like confusion.
Wanting happens due to the circumstance of feeling. And those people still have feeling. A mind that is fixing on something will remain stuck on something.
A mind that does not have emptiness will start up again even after it stops. It is like a deep meditation with no perceiving. Because of this, you should meditate on emptiness.
If you say that any speech found in a scripture was spoken by the Buddha, do you not agree that most of the Great Vehicle is equal to your teaching texts?
You say that leaving out one text makes them all faulty. But what if one is like a true teaching text? Why are they not all spoken by the Victorious One?
Even Mahakashyapa and others could not measure the depth of these words. Just because you do not understand them, who would make them unacceptable?
We want to help those who have suffering from confusion. So, we are freed from extreme clinging and fear. We can now stay in the cycle of rebirth. This is the result of emptiness.
You cannot succeed in proving wrong the position of emptiness. Therefore, without any doubt, you should meditate on emptiness.
There is a dark veil of troubling emotions and of things to know. Emptiness is the remedy for this darkness. If you wish to quickly become all-knowing, how could you not meditate on it?
If a thing produces suffering, fear will arise from it. But emptiness calms suffering. How could fear arise toward it?
If any self existed, a person might be afraid of anything. But since no self exists at all, who is there to be afraid?
Teeth, hair, and nails are not the self, and the self is not bones or blood. It is not mucus or phlegm, and it is not lymph or pus.
The self is not fat or sweat, and the lungs and liver are not the self. Other inside organs are also not the self, and the self is not feces or urine.
Flesh and skin are not the self, and warmth and wind are not the self. The openings of the body are not the self. In all ways, the six kinds of awareness are not the self either.
If the awareness of sound were lasting forever, it would hear sound all the time. If there is no thing to know, what does it know? Why would it be called an awareness?
If something that does not know anything were an awareness, then a piece of wood would be an awareness too. Therefore, it is certain that without a thing to know, there is no awareness.

If that exact same thing knows a shape, why does it not hear at the same time? Someone might say it is because a sound is not close by. But if that is true, then its awareness of the sound is gone too.
If something is made to notice a sound, how could it become the thing that notices a shape? One person can be labelled as both a father and a son. But that is not what is truly real.
So, brightness, restlessness, and darkness are neither a son nor a father. And the thing that notices a shape is not seen to have a nature that notices a sound.

Someone might say it is like an actor playing a new part. But if that thing changes, it is not lasting forever. If that new part is the exact same thing, then this kind of oneness is completely unheard of.
If that new part is not real, then tell me its own nature. If you say it is just awareness itself, then there is a problem. In that case, it would mean all people are exactly one person.
Things that can think and things that cannot think would also become one. This is because they both exist in the same way. When the differences between things are false, what makes them similar?
A thing without a mind is not the self. It is just like a vase. But you might say it knows things because it gets a mind. Then the thing that did not know anything before would be destroyed.
If the self never changes, what does the mind actually do to it? An unchanging self cannot know or do anything. That would make space into the self.
Someone might say: If the self does not exist, the link between action and result makes no sense. A person disappears after doing an action. So whose action will it be?
We both agree that the action and the result happen to different things. We also agree that the self does nothing here. So is this argument not pointless?
It is impossible to see the exact same person holding the cause and the result. We talk about a doer and one who experiences only because they are part of a single continuing stream.
A mind in the past or future is not the self, because it does not exist. But if the mind happening right now is the self, then when that mind disappears, there is no self either.
Think of a banana tree trunk. If you pull it apart piece by piece, nothing is left. It is the same when you look closely for a self. A real self cannot be found.
Someone might ask, "If there are no living beings, who should we show compassion to?" We show compassion to those imagined by our confusion. We accept this confusion for the sake of the result.

Someone might ask, "If there are no living beings, who gets the result?" That is true, but we only say someone gets it because of our confusion. Still, to calm suffering, we should not get rid of this confusion about the result.
Pride causes suffering. This pride grows from the confusion of a self. Someone might say we cannot get rid of this confusion either. But meditating on no separate self is the best way to stop it.
The body is not the feet or the lower legs. The thighs and the waist are not the body either. The belly and the back are not the body. The chest and the arms are not the body.

The ribs and the hands are not the body. The armpits and the shoulders are not the body. The organs inside are not the body either. If the head and the neck are not the body, then what exactly is the body?
If this body existed in all of these pieces through its different parts, the parts would just be in the parts. But where would the body itself be?
If the whole body existed in the hands and other parts, then however many hands and parts there are, there would be that many bodies.
If the body does not exist outside or inside, how does the body exist in the hands and other parts? If it is no different from the hands and other parts, how does it exist?

Therefore, there is no body. Because of confusion, the idea of a body comes up when looking at the hands and other parts. This happens because of their shape. It is just like mistaking a tree stump for a person.

As long as the gathering of circumstances lasts, the body appears like a person. In the same way, as long as those circumstances are present in the hands and other parts, the body appears to be there.
In the same way, what is the hand? It is just a collection of fingers. The finger is also a collection of joints. And a joint can be divided into its own parts.
For this very reason, we should use meditation on this careful thinking as a remedy. The calm focus that comes from looking closely is the food of the meditation master.
If there is a gap between the sense organ and the object, where would they meet? Even if there is no gap, they are just one thing. What would meet with what?
An atom does not enter another atom. It has no space inside, and they are equal. Without entering, there is no mixing. And without mixing, there is no meeting.
How could it make sense to say that something without parts can meet? If you have ever seen meeting and being without parts happen together, show it to me!
It does not make sense for awareness to meet anything, because it has no body. A gathering is also not a real thing, just as we saw before.
So, if touch does not exist, where would feeling come from? What is the point of all this hard work? What could possibly harm what?

Even a part is divided into tiny particles. That tiny particle is split into a part in one direction and another. But that split direction has no parts at all. It is just like space. So, even tiny particles do not really exist.
So, what wise person would hold onto a shape? A shape is just like a dream. When the body does not really exist like this, who is a man? And who is a woman?
If suffering is real, why does it not hurt people who are very joyful? If happiness is real, why do delicious foods not bring joy to people who are very sad?
Someone might say you do not have that experience because a stronger force covers it up. But if something is not an experience, how can it be a feeling?
Someone might say, "Suffering still exists in a faint form." Has its rough state not been removed? If you say, "It is just a different joy," then that faint form also belongs to that joy.
If suffering does not happen because an opposing circumstance comes up, does it not prove something? It shows that what we call a feeling is really just holding on to an idea.
There is no one who feels at all. Feeling does not really exist either. When we see this, why does our wanting not go away?
Seeing and touching are just like a dream or an illusion. Feeling happens at the exact same time as the mind. So, the mind cannot see that feeling.
A mind that comes before or after can only remember it, but cannot experience it. It cannot experience itself. Nothing else can experience it either.
There is no one who feels at all. Because of this, feeling does not really exist. So how could this harm a collection of parts with no separate self?
The mind does not live in a sense organ. It is not in a shape or anything like that, nor anywhere in between. The mind is not inside, and it is not outside. It cannot be found anywhere else either.
It is not the body, and it is not anywhere else. It is not mixed with anything, and it is not separate. It is nothing at all. Because of this, every living being is in freedom from sorrow by nature.
Right now, through everyday direct seeing, we can see all causes. Different things, like the parts of a lotus plant, are made by different causes.
If you ask what made those different causes, they come from the different causes that happened before them. Why is a cause able to make a result? It gets its power from the cause that came before it.
Someone might say a Creator is the cause of every being. First, tell me what this Creator is! If you say the Creator is just the elements, fine. But why tire yourself out arguing over a simple name?
But things like earth are many. They are not lasting, they do nothing on their own, and they are not holy. Since they are things we walk on and they are unclean, they are not the Creator.

The Creator is not space, because space does nothing. He is not the self, because I already proved that wrong. And if you say the maker of the world is beyond thought, what is the point of talking about something beyond thought?
Also, what do you claim he makes? Don't you say that the self, earth, and the true nature of the Creator are lasting forever? Awareness comes from a thing to know, and...
If awareness exists before the thing to know, what is it looking at? If awareness and the thing to know happen at the same time, what is it looking at?
But if awareness comes after the thing to know, what causes it? Because of this, we cannot see the coming into being of any things that appear.
Someone might say, "If everyday truth does not exist, how could there be the two truths? And if it relies on another everyday truth, how could living beings reach nirvana?"
This is just the busy thinking of someone else's mind. It is not my own everyday truth. If it is figured out later, it exists. If not, everyday truth simply does not exist.
Imagining and the thing imagined depend on each other. We can only share our careful examinations by relying on what people already know.
Someone might say, "If you test things with careful thinking that must also be tested, then that careful thinking has no end."
Happiness and suffering are without a beginning. They come from our actions. Tell me, what was made by him? If the cause is without a beginning, how can there be a beginning to the result?
Why does he not create things all the time? He does not depend on anyone else. If there is nothing else that he did not make, what would he depend on?

If he depends on things, then the gathering itself would be the cause. It would not be the Creator. When there is a gathering, there is no power to stop it from producing. Without it, there is no power to produce.
If the Creator acts without wanting to, he is controlled by another. Even if he wants to act, he depends on his own desire. If he acts like this, how is he the Creator?
People who believe in a never-changing atom have already been proven wrong. The Samkhya thinkers say that a never-changing Primal Matter is the cause of beings.
They say there are good qualities known as brightness, restlessness, and darkness. Their perfect balance is called Primal Matter. When they are out of balance, they are said to be beings.

When you look closely at the thing being examined, there is no support left for careful thinking. Because there is no support, careful thinking does not happen. That is what we call freedom from sorrow.
Some people say these two are true. That idea is very hard to defend. If an object exists through the power of awareness, what support is there for awareness itself?
But if awareness exists because of the thing to know, what support is there for the thing to know? If they exist because of each other, neither of them would exist.
If there is no father without a son, where does the son come from? Without a son, there is no father. In the same way, those two do not exist.

Someone might say, "A sprout grows from a seed. That very sprout lets us know the seed exists. Awareness comes from the thing to know. So why doesn't that awareness let us know the thing to know exists?"
If an awareness different from the sprout knows the seed exists, then an awareness is what knows the thing to know. But what lets us know that awareness itself exists?
It does not make sense for one thing to have three natures. So, it does not exist. In the same way, the good qualities do not exist. That is because they each have three parts too.
If the good qualities do not exist, things like sound cannot exist either. A piece of clothing is a thing without a mind. So, it is impossible for happiness and other feelings to exist in it.
If things have the nature of their cause, haven't we already looked closely at this? You say your cause is just happiness and other feelings. But cloth and other things do not come from happiness.
You might say happiness and other feelings come from things like cloth. Since those things do not exist, happiness does not exist either. Also, we never see happiness as something never-changing.
If happiness is showing itself, why do you not notice the feeling? If that same thing becomes fine, how can it be both rough and fine?
Because it stops being rough and becomes fine, both the fine and the rough are not lasting. In the same way, why do you not agree that all things are not lasting?
Think of a son dying in a dream. The busy thinking that he does not exist blocks the idea that he exists. But that is also false.
By looking closely, nothing at all exists without a cause. It also does not stay inside circumstances. This is true for one circumstance or many together.
It does not come from somewhere else. It does not stay, and it does not go away. Confusion makes it seem true. How is it different from an illusion?
Think about anything made by an illusion. Think about anything made by causes. Where did it come from? Where does it go? Look closely at this!
Sometimes a thing is seen only because something else is near. When that other thing is gone, it is not seen. It is made up, just like a reflection. How could being truly real happen in that?
If a thing already exists, why does it need a cause? But even if it does not exist, why does it need a cause?
If the rough thing is the same as happiness, then clear happiness is not lasting. Someone might say that a non-existent thing cannot arise because it is non-existent.
But a clear thing still arises even if it was non-existent before. This is true even if you disagree. If the result already lives inside the cause, a person eating food would be eating filth.
Use the money for a cotton cloth to buy cotton seeds and wear them! The world might not see this because of confusion. But people who know the way things really are say it is true.
The world also has this knowledge. Since it exists, why is it not seen? If the world is not a reliable way of knowing, then seeing a clear thing is also false.
Someone might ask: If a reliable way of knowing is actually wrong, is what it measures false? If so, meditation on emptiness would not make sense.
Without touching a made-up thing, we cannot notice its non-existent thing. Therefore, if an object is false, its non-existent thing is also clearly false.
Even millions of causes cannot change a non-existent thing. How could a non-existent thing ever become real? And what else could become a thing?
If a thing cannot exist when it does not exist, when will it ever become a thing? Until a thing is made, it cannot separate from being a non-existent thing.
If it does not separate from being a non-existent thing, there is no chance for a thing to exist. A thing also cannot become non-existent. If it did, it would have two natures.
So, there is no stopping, and there is no thing. Therefore, all these beings are always never born and never ending.
Beings are like a dream. When we look closely, they are like a banana tree. In the way things really are, there is no difference between finding freedom from sorrow and not finding it.
Since things are empty, what is there to gain and what is there to lose? What does it matter if someone honors you or treats you badly?
In that place, the ocean of suffering is huge and too hard to bear. It has no edge. There, people have very little strength, and their lives are short.
Even there, we get tired just trying to stay alive and healthy. We suffer from hunger, sleep, and being hurt. We also waste time being around foolish people.
Life passes by fast and has no meaning. Careful thinking is very hard to find. Since we are so used to distraction there, how can we ever stop it?
Even there, Mara works hard to make us fall into the great unhappy realm. There are many wrong paths, and it is hard to overcome even doubt.

Once again, the freedom to practice is hard to find. It is very hard to find a time when a Buddha appears. The river of troubling emotions is hard to leave behind. Sadly, suffering will just keep going on and on!
Even though they suffer so much, some beings do not see their own pain. We should feel very sad for those who live in the river of suffering!
For example, some people wash themselves again and again, but then walk right back into a fire. In the same way, some people live in terrible pain but still think they are happy.
Some people act as if there is no growing old and dying. First they will be killed. Then they will take a terrible fall into an unhappy realm.
When will I use a rain of my own happiness to bring peace to those burning in the fire of suffering? This rain will fall from clouds made of my store of goodness.
When will I respectfully build up my gathered store of goodness while not fixing on anything? And when will I teach emptiness to those who are ruined by fixing on something?
From Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero, this is the ninth chapter, called the Perfection of Wisdom.
Chapter Ten: Sharing the Goodness
Where do happiness and suffering come from? What is there to be upset or happy about? If I look for the way things really are, who is wanting? And what are they wanting?
If I look closely at this world of living beings, who will die here? What will happen, and what has happened? Who is a relative, and who is a friend?
I hope people like me completely understand that everything is like space. People who want happiness for themselves find causes for fighting and excitement.
They get very upset and very happy. With sadness, hard work, and arguing, they cut and pierce each other. Through harmful deeds, they live a very hard life.

They come to happy realms again and again, enjoying a lot of happiness. But after they die, they fall into the sufferings of the unhappy realms. These sufferings are terrible and last a very long time.

In life, there are many steep cliffs. There, what is not the way things really are is like this. Because things clash with each other there, in life there is no such thing as the way things really are.
I have written this book about the way of acting for awakening. By this good deed, may every being begin the way of acting for awakening.
There are beings everywhere sick with suffering in their bodies and minds. By my store of goodness, may they find an ocean of happiness and joy.
As long as they remain in the cycle of rebirth, may they never lose their happiness. May every being reach the unbroken happiness of an awakening hero.
There are many hells in the world realms. May every being with a body there rejoice with the happiness of Sukhavati.
May those hurt by cold find warmth. Endless rivers flow from the great clouds of the awakening heroes. May those rivers cool everyone hurt by heat.
May the forest of sword leaves become a thick sandalwood forest for them. May the trunks of the Shalmali trees also grow into wish-granting trees.
Even there, we spend our time just trying to stay alive and healthy. We get tired from hunger, sleep, and being hurt. We also waste time with foolish persons.
May everyone without clothes find something to wear. May the hungry find food. May the thirsty find water and delicious drinks.
May poor people find wealth. May very sad people find joy. May those who feel hopeless get their spirit back and become perfectly strong.
May all sick living beings get well quickly. May the sicknesses of all beings go away and never come back.
May terrified people become brave. May trapped people be set free. May weak people become strong. May everyone be kind and gentle to each other.
May all travelers be safe everywhere they go. Whatever they are traveling for, may they succeed without any trouble.
May people on boats and big ships succeed in what they plan to do. May they reach the shore safely and celebrate with their families.
May sweet songs of water birds like swans and geese make these places beautiful. May the regions of hell become wonderful. May they have lakes filled with sweet-smelling lotus flowers.

May the heaps of hot coals become heaps of jewels. May the burned ground become a smooth floor of crystal. May the mountains of the Crushing Hell become heavenly palaces of offerings. May they be filled with Well-Gone Ones.
May the rain of hot coals, burning stones, and weapons become a rain of flowers. Instead of striking each other with weapons, may they now toss flowers at each other in play.

Some beings are trapped in a fiery river that cannot be crossed. Their flesh is gone and their bones are the color of kunda flowers. By the power of my good deeds, may they get the bodies of gods. May they live with goddesses in a gently flowing river.

"Why are the men of Yama and the terrible crows and vultures so afraid? Whose great power chases away the dark and brings joy?" Thinking this, they look up and see blazing Vajrapani in the sky. May great joy free them from their harmful deeds. May they go with him.

A rain of flowers and sweet-smelling water falls. The fires and hot coals of hell go out with a hiss. Wondering, "Where does this sudden happiness come from?" may the hell beings look up and see Padmapani.

"Friends, throw away your fear and come quickly to us! His power frees us from all suffering and brings us joy. He protects all beings. He has the awakening mind and compassion. Who is this glowing boy with a topknot coming to make us fearless?"

"Look at him! The crowns of a hundred gods bow to his feet. His eyes are wet with compassion, and a rain of flowers falls on his head. He has beautiful palaces and thousands of goddesses singing his praise!" When they see Manjushri like this, may the hell beings shout with joy.

Through my roots of good deeds, may the living beings of hell see Samantabhadra and other awakening heroes. These heroes bring happy clouds and let a cool, sweet-smelling rain fall. When the living beings see this, may they be filled with joy.
May animals be free from the fear of eating each other. Just like the people of Uttarakuru, may the hungry ghosts be happy.
A stream of milk flows from the hands of the noble Avalokiteshvara. May this milk satisfy the hungry ghosts. After bathing in it, may they always stay cool.
May the blind see with their eyes. May the deaf always hear sounds. Just like Mayadevi, may pregnant women give birth safely without any harm.
May those who are lost on lonely paths meet fellow travelers. May they walk easily and not get tired. May they have no fear of robbers or tigers.
May the gods protect children, old people, and anyone without help in scary, wild places. May the gods also protect those who are asleep or drunk.
May everyone be free from any state without freedom. May they have trust, wisdom, and compassion. May they have perfect food and act well. May they always remember their past lifetimes.
May everyone have endless things to enjoy, just like the treasure house of space. May they live freely, without any fighting or harm.
May any living beings who lack brightness shine with great brightness. May any persons of hard practice who look weak get beautiful and perfect bodies.
May all the women in the world become men. May lowly people reach high places, but may their pride be defeated.
Through my store of goodness, may every living being stop doing harmful deeds. May they always do good deeds instead.
May they never lose the awakening mind. May they always practice the way of acting for awakening. May the Buddhas hold them close, and may they give up the actions of Mara.
May all those living beings live for a very long time. May they always be happy. May the sound of death never even be heard.
May every place be filled with beautiful wish-granting trees. May these places be full of Buddhas and children of the Buddhas sharing the sweet teachings.
Everywhere, may the ground be free of pebbles. May it be as flat as the palm of a hand. May it be made of soft lapis lazuli.
In every circle of followers, may there be many awakening heroes. May their wonderful goodness make the earth beautiful, and may they stay there forever.
May all beings with a body hear the sound of the teachings without ever stopping. May they hear it from birds, from trees, from rays of light, and even from the sky.
May they always meet the Buddhas and the children of the Buddhas. May they bring endless clouds of offerings to the teacher of beings.
May the gods send rain at the right time. May the harvests be plentiful. May kings act according to the teachings. May the world also flourish.
May medicines be strong. May the recitation of secret sacred words be successful. May sky-goers, demons, and others like them have minds full of compassion.
May no living being suffer. May they never be afraid or looked down upon. May no one ever be unhappy.
May monasteries stand strong, beautiful with reading and reciting. May the community of monks and nuns always live in harmony. May the goals of the community of monks and nuns be achieved.
May monks who want to train find solitude. May they leave every distraction behind and meditate with ready minds.
May nuns have everything they need. May they stop arguing and causing harm. After becoming a monk or nun, may no one ever lose their good conduct.
May those who have broken their good conduct get tired of it. May they wipe away all their harmful deeds. After they reach a happy realm, may their strict practice stay strong even there.
May wise persons be honored and receive alms. May their continuing stream be completely pure. May they become famous everywhere.
May they never feel the suffering of the unhappy realms. Even without hardship, may they have bodies better than the gods. May they quickly become Buddhas.
May all living beings make offerings to all the Buddhas again and again. Through the wonderful happiness of the Buddhas, may they always be filled with happiness.
May the awakening heroes do what they plan for the good of others. Whatever the Protectors wish for, may living beings receive it.
In the same way, may the self-awakened ones and the Hearers also be happy.
Because of Manjushri's kindness, may I always remember my past lifetimes. May I remember them until I reach the Ground of Perfect Joy, and may I succeed in becoming a monk or nun.
Even with only simple food, may I be strong and full of life. In all my lifetimes, may I find the perfect chance to live in a quiet place.
Whenever I want to see him or ask a small question, may I see the Protector Manjushri himself. May nothing ever stand in my way.
I want to help every living being across space in the ten directions. Just as Manjushri acts, may my way of acting be exactly like his.
As long as space remains, and as long as beings remain, may I also stay. May I stay to clear away the suffering of beings.
Whatever the suffering of beings may be, let it all fall on me. Through the community of awakening heroes, may beings enjoy happiness.
The Buddha's teaching is the only medicine for the suffering of beings. It is the source of all happiness. May the Buddha's teaching remain for a long time, along with gain and respect.
A good thinking mind comes from his kindness. I bow down to Manjushri. I have grown because of his kindness. I also bow down to the good friend.
The tenth chapter, called sharing the goodness, from Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero.
