Translator's Note
First, it was checked and finished by the Indian teacher who ordained me, Sarvajnadeva, and the chief editor-translator, Bande Paltsek. They used a copy from Kashmir.

Later, it was fixed, translated, and finished by the Indian teacher who ordained me, Dharmashribhadra, and the chief editor-translators Rinchen Zangpo and Shakya Lodro. They matched it to a copy and an explanation from the central land.
Even later, it was carefully fixed, translated, and perfectly finished by the Indian teacher who ordained me, Sumatikirti, and the chief editor-translator, the monk Loden Sherab.
The Thus-Gone One himself explained this. He gave the reasons for it in the teaching called the Question of Subahu. He said this to help living beings whose wishes are still small.
Imagine if just one of these illnesses could destroy all the people living in Jambudvipa. And imagine if no medicine to cure them could be found anywhere.
If even soldiers fight enemies who will die anyway, and ignore the suffering of being struck by arrows and spears, and do not run away before they reach their goal...
I should take away the suffering of others, because it is suffering, just like my own suffering. I should help others because they are living beings, just like my own body.

Someone might ask, "Why should we stop the suffering of everyone?" There is no room to argue. If we stop it, we must stop it for all. If not, then my own suffering should not be stopped either, since I am a living being just like them.
By getting used to it, I take the drops of seed and blood from others as "I". Even though they are without a thing, I still call them "I".
In the same way, the fire of hatred spreads to whatever the mind is clinging to. To stop my store of goodness from burning, I must throw away right now whatever my mind is clinging to.
I might think, "I am afraid to give away my arms and legs." But this fear is just confusion. I am not weighing what matters more and what matters less.
At first you worked hard to lift that face. Even when you lifted it up, it looked down shyly. Whether you had seen it before or not, that face was covered by a cloth.
For things that are free of blame, which are in my hands and in the hands of living beings, I must always hold my mind like a magical creation, with no 'I' in it.
My mind, you hold onto this body and call it 'mine.' But why do you guard it so closely? If you and the body are separate, what can it really do for you?
Anger is an enemy, and it brings these and other kinds of suffering. Whoever tries hard to destroy anger will be happy in this life and the next.
See a lower person and others as yourself. Then see yourself as them. Clear your mind of busy thinking. Practice feeling jealousy, rivalry, and pride.
Someone might say, "Because the mind uses other circumstances to see, it shines to itself." Using magic eye ointment lets you see a vase. But it does not let you see the eye ointment itself.
Someone might ask, "If the Great Vehicle is not proven, how is your sacred text proven?" The answer is, "Because it is proven for both of us." But at first, it was not proven for you.
For the sake of those who experience suffering from confusion, a person who is free from the extremes of clinging and fear can stay in the cycle of rebirth. This is the result of emptiness.
If something has the nature of noticing a sound, how could it become the thing that notices a shape? One person can be labelled as both a father and a son. But that is not what is truly real.
Someone might ask, "If there are no living beings, who should we show compassion to?" We show compassion to those imagined by our confusion. We accept them for the sake of the result.
It is like the fire at the end of time. It completely burns up great harmful deeds in a single instant. The wise Protector Maitreya explained its endless benefits to Sudhana.
From the moment you truly take up this mind to completely free the endless realm of living beings, with a mind of never turning back,
Other beings do not have this wish even for themselves. But this wish to help every living being is born as a brand new wonder. It is an amazing jewel of a mind.
For beings who have no happiness and face so much suffering, this mind fills them with happiness and cuts through all their suffering.
I have no store of goodness, and I am very poor. I have no other wealth to offer. Therefore, may the Protectors who care about the good of others accept this for my sake by their own power.
Ignorance confused me completely. I used to feel joy in my mistakes. Now I see these mistakes. I own up to them to the Protectors from the bottom of my heart.
I will die before the cleansing of my harmful deeds. Please protect me quickly so I can have sure freedom from them.

In the same way, the teachings they have realized are what I go to for shelter. These teachings chase away the fears of the cycle of rebirth. The group of awakening heroes is also who I go to for shelter.

This free and fortunate life is very hard to find. We have gained what we need to reach the purpose of a human life. If we do not use this life to do what is helpful, how will we ever find a life like this again?
People who want to end the hundreds of sufferings of life, to take away the sadness of living beings, and to enjoy hundreds of joys should never give up the awakening mind.

As soon as the awakening mind is born, in a single moment, poor beings trapped in the prison of the cycle of rebirth will be called children of the Well-Gone Ones. The whole world, including gods and humans, will bow down to them.

The one leader of travelers for all beings has a limitless mind. He looked at it closely and saw how precious it is. Because of this, anyone who wants to be free from the realms of beings should hold tightly to the precious awakening mind.
What if someone has a hateful thought toward such a kind child of the Victorious Ones? The Sage taught that they will stay in hell for one great age for every hateful thought.

I bow down to the body of anyone in whom this supreme, precious mind has arisen. Even if someone hurts them, they still connect that person to happiness. I go for shelter to these sources of happiness.

I offer sweet smells and incense from the worlds of gods and others. I offer wish-granting trees and jewel trees. I offer crops that grow without anyone ploughing the field. I offer every other beautiful thing that is worthy of being offered.

In my mind, I gather all these things. I offer them to the Sages, the best of beings, and to their children. They are the greatest ones worthy of gifts. May those of great compassion think of me with love and accept my offerings.
Because of his compassion, his actions never go wrong. I cry out in a sad voice to the protector Avalokiteshvara. I say, "Please protect me, one who has done harmful deeds!"
In the past, I went against your commands. Now I have seen great fear. You are the one I go to for shelter. Please take away my fears quickly!
In that case, for the All-Knowing Doctor who takes away all pain, not wanting to follow his commands is extreme ignorance. Anyone who ignores him should be scolded.
We must be careful even near a small, normal cliff. So of course we must be careful when we could fall a thousand leagues into a drop that lasts a very long time!
I put my hands together and pray to the Victorious Ones who wish to pass into freedom from sorrow. Do not leave these beings in blindness. Please stay with us for countless great ages.
Just as the Well-Gone Ones of the past created the awakening mind and, step by step, followed the trainings of the awakening heroes,
In the same way, I will create the awakening mind to help all beings. Step by step, I will also practice the trainings.
Now I must do whatever I can to act in a way that fits this family. I will make sure I never stain this flawless and noble family.
Suppose you decide in your mind to give away a small, ordinary thing. If you do not give it, the teachings say you will become a hungry ghost.
Even destroying the happiness of one living being would bring my own ruin. So how much worse to destroy the happiness of beings with bodies, who fill all of space to its very edge!
Because of this, I must respectfully do what I vowed. If I do not make an effort starting today, I will go lower and lower.
A Thus-Gone One appearing is very rare. Getting a human body, having trust, and being ready to do good deeds are also rare. When will I ever get these things?
If I do not do good deeds and I pile up harmful deeds, I will not hear even the sound of the happy realms for a billion great ages.
If I kindly serve and honor others, they bring me help and happiness. But if I serve my troubling emotions, they bring me further suffering and harm.
My true natural enemies are the constant cause of all suffering. Today, I am trying hard to destroy them. So of course I will not lose heart, even if this fight brings me hundreds of sufferings.

Fishermen, outcasts, farmers, and others only think about making a living. Yet they put up with the pain of cold and heat. I am working for the happiness of all beings. Why should someone like me not endure these things too?

I promised to free the beings who fill space in the ten directions. I promised to free them from their troubling emotions. But when I made this promise, I was not even free from my own troubling emotions!
Since I do not even know what I can really do, am I not crazy to talk like this? So I will never turn back from destroying my troubling emotions.
I will hold tightly to this. I will hold a grudge and fight this battle! This is the only kind of troubling emotion I should not let go of, because it destroys all other troubling emotions.
Where could fish and other animals be put so they are never killed? The perfection of good conduct is explained as coming from getting the mind of giving up.
Wild living beings are like space. They can never be fully defeated. But if this single mind of anger is defeated, it is like defeating all those enemies at once.
It is better to lose my gain and honor. It is better to lose my body and the things I live on. It is even better to lose other good deeds. But I must never let my mind fail.
This gang of thieves, made of troubling emotions, looks for a chance to strike. When they find it, they steal my good deeds. They even destroy life in a happy realm.
For lucky people who act with respect because they are afraid to do wrong, keeping in mind grows easily. This happens by spending time with a teacher and listening to the teacher who ordained me.
If destroying the happiness of just one living being ruins me, what will happen if I destroy the happiness of endless beings with bodies who fill all of space? I do not even need to ask.

A good deed becomes very great when you do it with a strong, lasting wish, or when a remedy against troubling emotions moves you to act. This is true when you act toward people with good qualities, people who help you, and those in suffering.

People who are ready for the vast teachings should not practice the lesser teachings instead. Good behavior should not be given up completely. I should not lure people away with teaching texts and sacred words.
I should not be alone with another woman in a vehicle, on a bed, on a seat, or in a room. By watching and asking, I should find out what makes the world lose faith. Then I must avoid all of it.
Whether directly or indirectly, I should only do things that help living beings. For the sake of living beings alone, I should give everything to awakening by sharing the goodness.

When I am caught up in danger, a festival, and the like, if I cannot keep up my practice, I should act at ease. It is taught that at times of giving, good conduct should be treated with even-mindedness.
If I want gain, honor, or fame, or want to seek helpers and followers, or if my mind wants to be served, at that time I should stay like a log.
If I feel impatience, laziness, fear, rudeness, or idle talk, or if my mind clings to my own side, at that time I should stay like a log.

So I will practice being in control of myself. I will always keep a smiling face. I will completely stop frowning and scowling. I will be a friend to all beings who wander through life, and speak honestly.
I should learn how to rely on a teacher from the life story of Shrisambhava. I should read the scriptures to learn this and other things the Buddha taught.
Think of snakes, biting flies, itchy rashes, and the feeling of hunger and thirst. The suffering they bring is pointless. Why do you not see this?
Even when suffering happens, wise people keep a clear mind. This is because they are fighting a war against troubling emotions, and many harms happen during a battle.
Suffering also has a good quality. Getting tired of suffering stops us from feeling superior. We feel compassion for those in the cycle of rebirth. We avoid harmful deeds and enjoy good deeds.
Everything is controlled by other forces. Because of this power, everything is powerless. Knowing this, a person will not get angry at any things. They are like things that magic has conjured up.
Someone might ask, "What can stop what? Even stopping things makes no sense!" But because suffering depends on its causes, it does make sense. It is not wrong to wish for suffering to be cut away.
Therefore, if you see an enemy or a friend doing something wrong, think, "This has come from these circumstances." Think this way and stay at ease.
Someone might hit me with a stick. If I feel anger at the person swinging it, since he is driven by hatred too, it makes more sense to feel anger at hatred.
If my intention has a good quality, I will not go to hell. If I protect myself, what will happen to them here?

You feel no sorrow for the harmful deeds you yourself have done. On top of that, do you want to compete with others who have built up a store of goodness? This is the end of the second part of the book.
Even if I knew my own good, what own good is there in that? If I only want my mind to feel happy, I would also have to turn to gambling, alcohol, and things like that.
Therefore, some people are around to destroy my praise and things like it. Are they not protecting me from falling into an unhappy realm?
So, practice being in control of oneself and always keep a smiling face. Stop frowning and scowling completely. Be a friend to wandering beings and speak honestly.
If even a tiny part of that special collection of supreme good qualities appears in someone, I should make offerings to them. Even giving them the three realms would be too little.
There are true friends who never trick me and who help me in ways I cannot measure. How could I ever pay them back? The only way is by making living beings happy.
When the Lord of Death suddenly arrives, I will find that "This is not done. That is just begun. This is only half done." Then I will think, "Oh no, I am ruined!"
In this life, you flip around in fear like a live fish. Since you have done harmful deeds, there is no need to even mention the unbearable sufferings of hell!
If my own faults stop me from practicing patience with this, I am only making a block, even when the cause of a store of goodness is right in front of me.
A beggar who arrives at the right time is not a block to giving. Someone who gives you the vows of a monk or nun cannot be called a block to becoming a monk or nun.
Therefore, patience arises by depending on someone's very hateful mind. Since they are the exact cause of patience, they deserve to be honored just like the holy teachings.

Living beings have a share in bringing about the qualities of a Buddha. Because of this, living beings and the Buddhas are seen as equal. But no one is truly equal to the Buddhas. They have an endless ocean of good qualities.

If I get used to giving up, it will happen in another life too. My harmful deeds and suffering will increase. Any other action, and the time of its result, will become weak. Then that other action will not get finished either.
I should build my pride in three things: my action, my power over troubling emotions, and my ability. Thinking, "I will do this alone," is pride in action.
If we never get enough of our desires for pleasure, which are like honey smeared on a razor's edge, how could I ever get enough of a store of goodness? Its ripening is happiness and peace.
Just like an experienced warrior clashing swords with enemies on a battlefield, I must dodge the weapons of the troubling emotions. Then I must strike to destroy those enemy troubling emotions.
Think of flies, gadflies, bees, and worms. If even they build up the power of joyful effort, they will reach the highest awakening, which is very hard to achieve.
The power of the awakening mind uses up past harmful deeds. It also gathers an ocean of stored goodness. Because of this, the bodhisattva is greater than the Hearers.
I must build up many good qualities in myself and others. If I must practice each and every good quality for an ocean of great ages,
Because I did not have a strong wish for the teachings in the past, and still do not have it now, I have ended up in such a sad, empty state. Who would ever give up a strong wish for the teachings?
From Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero, this is the seventh chapter, called the Teaching on Joyful Effort.
If we do not see them, we feel no joy, and the mind cannot become a settled mind. Even when we do see them, we are never satisfied. We are still hurt by wanting, just as before.
If I share the same fate as a childish person, I will certainly go to an unhappy realm. If they lead me to a fate unlike that of the noble ones, what is the use of relying on a childish person?

If I spend time with a childish person, I will hear them praising themselves and putting others down. They will talk happily about the cycle of rebirth. Every kind of bad deed will surely come from this.
Because they will not do me any good, and I will not do them any good either, we will only ruin ourselves.
A bee just takes nectar from a flower. In the same way, I will only take what helps me practice the teachings. I will not become close to anyone, as if I had never seen them before.
Living beings have many different strong wishes. If even the Victorious Ones cannot please them all, how could someone as lowly as me do it? Therefore, I will let go of my thoughts about the world.
In the past, you sent many messengers and made many requests for their sake. You did not hesitate to do harmful deeds or ruin your good name for them.
You are full of filth yourself. You use it all the time. Yet you still want other bags of filth. You desire them out of greed for filth.
You do not even look down on your own filth. But out of greed for filth, you also desire another bag of filth.

Even a ten-millionth part of that hardship could bring us to the state of a Buddha. A person full of desire goes through greater suffering than the way of acting for awakening. Yet they get no awakening at all.
They act on their own without clinging and are not tied to anyone at all. The joy of being happy with enough is hard even for Indra to find.
If I do not truly exchange my own happiness for the suffering of others, I will never reach the state of a Buddha. Even in the cycle of rebirth, I will find no happiness.
Out of confusion, I cause suffering to others. This brings me unbearable suffering, and I throw away the perfect joy that brings happiness I can see and cannot see.
In short, whatever harm you have done to others for your own sake, let that same harm fall upon yourself, for the sake of all living beings.
Even when I tell you what to do, if you, my mind, do not act that way, I must defeat you. All faults rely on you, so I have no other choice.
A continuing stream and a collection of parts are not real in themselves. They are like a necklace or an army. Since no one truly owns suffering, who is there to control it?
If facing one single suffering removes many other sufferings, a kind person should certainly take on that suffering for themselves and others.
When living beings are freed, there is an ocean of joy. Is that joy not enough? What is the use of wanting freedom?
If I wish to be great myself, I will be reborn in an unhappy realm as someone low and foolish. If I shift that wish to others, I will gain a happy realm and respect.

If I spend time with a childish person, bad deeds will definitely happen. That childish person brings about praising oneself and putting others down. We will talk about enjoying the cycle of rebirth and things like that.
That past time when you ruined me is over. Now I see you. Where will you go? I will destroy all of your feeling superior.
In that way, you have handed me over again and again. I have suffered for a long time. I remember those grudges. Now I will destroy your thoughts about your own good.
So, without being attached, I will give up my body to help others. It has many faults. Still, I will keep it like a tool for getting things done.

Meditation masters are not all equal in their thinking minds. A higher master proves a lower one wrong. They use examples they both agree on. They do not question these examples because they just want a result.
